This is a thread I don't type easily.  I want this to be about how strong this community truly is and that I not only recognize that but I also do what I can to nourish and encourage it.  With that being said recently there has been posts stating that HF has seen an increase in LQP. I have mixed feelings about that as a fact because I haven't really witnessed it.  So maybe it's true, but maybe it's not.

For me it appears the Lounge is fairly active lately, which is not or has ever been a high-quality section on HF.  Other sections are less active but that doesn't really mean we have a quality problem per se. I think it's more of a post quantity problem.

Another repeated complaint is that reputations used to mean something and now they don't.  It's very true that reps mean less than they did before. This is intentional.  And while you might ask why bother keeping them, it's because I still believe it's a feature this community can utilize again but in a different way.  I do not have a direct plan on what those changes will be for reputations or when it will be implemented. I am still considering a few ideas and working out methods for new features on HF that use reps in a meaningful way.  It will come, just give us time.  

I view the community aspect of HF as very important.  Everyone sees some of the recent changes as an attempt to make HF marketplace centric.  This is only a partial-truth.  The HF Marketplace is an important aspect of this site and one that I continue to cultivate and improve.  The new changes were long-overdue but it's not easy to balance changes to the market and the community equally. At times it could appear that one is more important than the other but that is not the truth. 

The majority of my plan to transform the HF community revolves around Bytes.  I'm going to implement features on HF that will use the Bytes in ways you'll not expect.  Interaction between members using Bytes is fairly high priority for development.

Right now Xerotic and iHydra are working hard to complete the mobile theme.  Contracts is mainly done.  I'm moving us to a new server soon.  We will be implementing APIv2 on the new server. Bytes are working great.  The site actually is in an amazing place right now.  

Some complain that reps were the rewards system for high quality.  I can respect that view but I don't really share it. I think reps were used for market, for abuse, for harassing, and sometimes for quality posting reward. Overall reps were used in so many ways that it was really confusing what a high rep meant.  I'd love to see that a high reputation means you're a great member. So how do we get there?  I have some ideas on that but nothing solid enough to implement or to actually post in public.

As for Bytes. I have some amazing ideas and basically I'm waiting for the current workload to be completed before taking on the task of development.  I'll try not to go directly into details but conceptually I plan on having more games and activities on-site related to Bytes.  And, no, that doesn't mean gambling even though there will be some of that added including a Blackjack very soon.  My plan is going to be adding a way for members to compete against each other using Bytes.  

https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=5833328 

That threads was before we implemented Bytes btw.  Maybe now some of this is starting to make sense to members.  

Don't give up on this community nor allow disgruntled members to disuade you into believing things that aren't true about HF.  Your Admin team has a lot of work to accomplish but please be fair to us and let us complete our work before you criticize what we're trying to do. You can't say you don't like someone cooking while it's on the stove.  You have to wait till it's on the plate.  

Thank you.

I'll try and keep this brief and low-drama.  I want it public so that Phixel can see I'm not afraid of providing the truth of the story.

https://hackforums.net/member.php?action=profile&uid=3021787

So he was one of a few members who contacted me about creating an HF theme.  After asking him to show me examples of his work and a couple PMs I provided him access to KnotBB.com (our test development site) to work on a theme. Progress seemed to go well enough. At one point a couple weeks into his work he moaned about being broke. I sent him a $50 and $200 BTC payment as a courtesy for the work he did so far. As a token of appreciation. Mind you he told me he would do the theme for free and he just wanted to help.  But I was happy to pay him a bit as I know he was trying his best.  

At some point I needed to place that theme on HF as a secondary and work on it directly from Admin CP.  I discussed giving him and Xerotic ACP access to really push development.  Xerotic has been here forever.  Phixel had much less history.  I felt more comfortable asking him for valid proof of identity before granting him ACP.  

He sent me a very old passport image from when he was a child.  I could hardly believe his story that he told me that was all the identity he had.  Seemed very strange to me.  I became very uncomfortable with giving him ACP access and told him so.  I later decided he would not get ACP access and that's when it got weird.  

He sent me some PMs that imho showed emotional instability.  He was someone I no longer wanted to work with.  A few PMs continued to come from him and I tried to keep my responses brief and professional.  I didn't want to seem ungrateful for his efforts. But eventually I snapped and sent him this:

[quote=Omni]This feels awkward and it shouldn't. You say you're a person and not a computer. Well, that may be true but we're not best friends and I don't know you. So while you are a person, you're a person I don't know very much about.

You're trying to force me into a conversation. You want me to communicate to you like a person.

Sure, let's go for it.

I don't trust you at all. I think you're a liar. I think you have a hidden agenda and I don't trust anything you tell me. You say things about your mom which makes you sound like a kid then you talk about having a son. You seem incredibly suspicious to me. All the conversations I have had with you seem to make you an unstable person mentally and I don't need that as part of my work day. I especially don't need it for an admin or site staff.

I saw at Knot that you downloaded the files after we had our talk where I told you that I wasn't going to make you admin. Not a lot of legit reason for you to do that imho. Certainly not the actions of someone I should trust. Since that conversation you've done very little an emotionally you are constantly questioning me and our relationship. You obviously don't know how to handle this.

You're not mature enough. You're not steady enough. You're not trusted enough.

I'm pissed I paid you anything because the work ain't done and I may end up scratching it all when I get a new designer which I've already started to work on. I should have waited to pay you.

We're not friends. We aren't even acquaintances because I don't know you at all.

Just remember, you asked for this. I'm sure your reply will piss me off enough that I'll close your account so consider what you say back to me carefully or better yet, don't reply at all. But I know types like you, you won't be able to resist the urge.

I was being kind to you and respectful. That's blown now. You can fuck off for all I care.

Now you feel like person? Hope you do.[/quote]

That was 5 months ago and he continued to act weird. I put him on my ignore list and avoided him. But he insisted on sending me contacts at odd times about weird things like I was talking about him. He got angry one day I think because I mentioned his username in a thread. Just oddball shit.  As that went on I had enough and just closed his account.  

I wasn't going to use the theme he worked on. I didn't think it was finished enough and Xerotic and I have explored premade premium themes from MyBB designers. I need someone with ACP access on HF to really get this done correctly because just installing a theme for the MyBB pages will not be enough. While working on KnotBB with Xerotic and seeing the multiple custom themes we have installed, I realize I liked the one Phixel worked on the most. It was the simplest feel and more of what I wanted to see on HF.  I contacted a couple designers on HF to see if anyone wanted to help finish it.  iHydra is currently helping us out and working to hopefully get the project back to where it was before all this drama.  We hope to install the theme on HF this week as a secondary then develop it and make it primary when ready.

message:
This is direct quote from the GDPR law.

[quote]However, the further retention of the personal data should be  lawful  where it  is  necessary,  for  exercising  the  right  of  freedom of  expression and information, for compliance  with  a  legal  obligation,  for  the  performance  of  a  task  carried  out  in  the  public interest  or  in  the exercise  of  official authority  vested in  the  controller,  on  the  grounds of  public interest  in  the  area  of  public health, for  archiving purposes in  the  public interest, scientific or historical  research purposes or  statistical purposes, or for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims. [/quote]

This is in a nutshell why we're not going to just delete accounts.  We have a legal obligation to retain data.  There is also archival purpose and freedom of expression.  

I'm getting contacts requesting accounts deletions.  We are not going to do it and under GDPR we have exemptions that directly apply to our community.

There might be some situations though where accounts might get altered or posts edited/deleted.  We've always been against the posting of private data but there have been threads where members were asked to post their social media accounts or emails in contests and giveaways.  Those may get deleted if requested.  We don't agree with situations where members exposed their private information on the forum but now GDPR makes it a legal issue.

We are going to be as compliant as possible, if not fully compliant.  We're almost done with the export feature.  

I thank everyone who is bearing with us at this time and if you have questions or concerns I'm happy to try and discuss the situation. It's a complex law and we're a complex site.  Unfortunately this is so new that many sites haven't done anything to be compliant and there aren't many sites like HF which we can draw examples from.  I do hope that HF is the site that sets the example and we're working hard to make that happen.

Thank you.

btw, if you wish to read the GDPR yourself then go for it:
https://gdpr-info.eu/

message:
In order to provide information on the recent reputation reset I'm creating this post. It should answer any important questions you may have.

Recently we've added a new Marketplace system called Contracts along with Marketplace Suite.  These are going to be the driving force behind our market.  When we launched Contracts we removed the display of reputation inside Market tab.  This caused some confusion for members who wanted to still see reps.  Our new system is replacing reputations for market activity.  

Previously the reputation system was the main method used to vouch for members or make complaints.  Yet it was a far from perfect system. In MyBB, our forum software, reputations were never intended to be used for marketplace style comments. We did our best but it was highly flawed.  Many left "deal with caution" reputations to members they never dealt with. And friends would often vouch for friends without dealing with them. It was often difficult to use reputations as a means to trust a member.

Contracts was conceived by me many years ago and called "Vouch" but unfortunately I was never able to realize that feature until this year with the help of Xerotic, our new admin.  And this whole time reputations have built up as a psuedo-trust system.  Almost daily there was abuse and complaints about reputations.  

With Contracts we no longer have to rely on reputations and we encouraged those active in the Marketplace to immediately begin using Contracts. However, when we released it, it was was completely obvious that members were resistent to the change and adoption of the new system.  That was a serious problem and the only true solution was a complete reset of all reputations for all members.  

While it may seem drastic and disheartning to lose years of reputations we have to embrace changes to the site which improve our features and functions.  We also can't anchor ourselves to old ways especially if they didn't work very well.   We needed to do it even if members don't agree.  

Some are concerned about their old reps and associations with friends.  We plan on putting the old reputations on HF in archived form for you to view. No one but you and our Staff/Admin team will be able to see those reputations.  

We also changed our reputation system to be canned pre-written messages.  You will no longer be able to write custom comments on reps.  This prevents all forms of abuse and stop the reputations from being used as a marketplace trust tool.  Again, something that was necessary. 

Since we have revamped how reputation works on the site it was decided that the old rules for reputation no longer applied.  The Help Docs were updated to reflect that.  New policies include allow asking for reputations or even selling/buying it.  Also enabled is the ability to link reps to a post.  That ability allows you to rep a member twice in fact, once from profiles and once from a post.  We encourage you to read our Help Doc for more info.

We expect reputations to still have a place here on HF but only as a community based system and not marketplace.  We have no plans to remove or disable the reputation system.

I hope this has answered many of the questions. If you see others asking about reps please link them to this thread. Thank you.

message:
I hate having to type these up sometimes.  

First off, I'm feeling under-the-weather.  I'm a bit ill, headache, sore throat, and cough.  I just don't feel very good at all.

This morning I got up around 9pm.  For the second day in a row it appeared the server went offline for 30 minutes from midnight to 12:30am which is when there are some cron jobs which restarts the server and does some log rotating.  I figured I would look into it and I took it as a good time to do some server updates.  

After running a couple updates, one of which was Apache, the HTTPD process wouldn't start. It gave me an APR error.

[quote]/usr/sbin/httpd: Undefined symbol "apr_bucket_alloc_aligned_floor"[/quote]

After some digging it appears to be related to the APR (Apache Portable Runtime) which is basically a set of tools for Apache.  Seems we have some issue on the server with our library and having the apache build properly.  Not a lot of help online related to the problem.  I did a lot of updating of various server packages and tried different configurations to get it working but nothing.  

And please note that I plan on moving us to a new server within the next week and so this failure on the old server was pushing me to just move on if I couldn't get it fixed right away.  I told myself I'd give it 3-4 hours and I would just give-up and move us.  A move at this time would mean 24-48 hours of downtime because I still have some configuring to do on the new server.  

So on top of all this I'm sick and rather upset that I have to deal with this crap right now.  If I was an employee instead of the boss I'd just call out sick and sit on the couch.  I really don't want to make any mistakes in the move or setting up the new server.  It requires 100% mental focus.  Something I do not have right now.

Well, after 4 hours and just about to give-up I got it working.  I basically removed ever single trace of the existing APR libs and on the next build of Apache it installed all the libs required without conflict.  So bingo, down for 4 hours but at least I don't have to move us yet.  

We will be moving soon and that will be a day of downtime.  

Sorry about this today.  Shit happens I suppose.  Still not sure if that midnight server crash is fixed or not either but I suppose we'll just live with it until we move.

New server has more resources and will not be FreeBSD.  I'm hoping it will be more stable and easier to configure and update.  

Thank you.

message:
As many know HF was started almost 11 years ago (Anniversary on April 21st).  Many don't know that in the early HF days I merged a couple other forum databases into HF.  Mainly this was to add content and it was never intended to add the users as active members.  In those days we didn't have the CLOSED group nor did I foresee a reason to ban all those accounts. I figured they would just be dormant. 

At some point in 2011 a portion of our database was dumped.  It was indeed the users table and so accounts were at risk of being stolen if anyone used simple passwords.  At the time I immediately had all upgraded accounts change their passwords and enforced a stricter password policy which is now a minimum 12 character with upper,lower, and digits requirement.  

Over the years that dump has been used to bruteforce the passwords of the registered accounts which weren't upgraded.  I eventually created the CLOSED group for a number of reasons one of which was to have a permanent group that does exactly what the group name suggests and closes the account.  It can still be logged into but it's a dead account with no access.

Members still to this day send me PMs with alarm that a dump exists and that there are thousands of accounts stolen.  This is not true.  The dump was almost completely useless.  Notice I said, "almost"....well I know a few accounts had slipped through the cracks of my queries and were still active.  Occasionally I'd see these 2008-2009 accounts suddenly become active and I'd review it and see it was indeed stolen at some point.  So that's how it's been for a few years.

April 12th, 2018 we had about 30,000 bot login attempts to these accounts.  This means those accounts the passwords were compromised.  But here is the good part.  My logs gave me everything I needed to track down all the stolen accounts and permanently close all of them. So thanks to whoever spent their time with this and helped me finally close them all. 

There was 300+ IPs from the botnet, they had 30,000 successful logins.  In those logins they gained access to 280 non-closed accounts.  Of those there was 2 Ub3r accounts, 12 L33t accounts, and the rest just regular members. 

Took me some time to gather logs, parse them, write up scripts, and execute everything without mistake but it's done now. All these accounts are permanently closed with no way to login to them or recover them.  All salts were randomly changed causing all future login attempts to fail.

This is an old thread I found talking about the dump.  So as you can see this has been a lingering issue since 2011.
https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=1414679

These accounts could be, and probably were, used for scamming. Pretty happy this is finally resolved.

Anyways, that's what I been up to the past couple days along with MyBB bug fixing and working with Xerotic. More to come.  :)

message:
I'd like to explain why we had about 24 hours of downtime and what exactly happened.

Since the upgrade to MyBB 1.8x a few things broke in the database. One of them was the mybb_posts table index for the 'message' column which is basically the posts.  Some of you recall that we were offline for 2 days for that fiasco.  Partially because some of the queries literally took 12-15 hours to complete.  The main issue is the size of the mybb_posts table itself which is stored as InnoDB but was indeed over 30Gb.  To run a query like an "ALTER TABLE mybb_posts" is the worst resource hog.  Not only does it take many hours to run but HF has to be shutdown to do it.  The table is locked for the query.   The ALTER TABLE in Innodb uses a TMP table and copies all the data there before committing the change.  So you can imagine on 30Gb table how long that can take.

So the message index was missing after the upgrade.  This mainly effected the search.  You should have notice that searching posts wasn't getting results because of resources I was forced to disable message searching and all searches were based only on thread titles.  InnoDB does support FULLTEXT searching which is great but the index does have to be created. Years ago InnoDB did not support FULLTEXT and so I used a custom plugin for SPHINX SEARCH and that worked extremely well up until we switched from 1.6x to 1.4x and then it started to falter.  Eventually the SPHINX SEARCH was breaking down mainly due to MyBB updates and incompatibilities.  I didn't mind because I knew that InnoDB was now supporting FULLTEXT. 

Some time ago we moved our database to a new server with more resources and I added the FULLTEXT while we were 1.6x. All was right with the world and truthfully HF ran very well on 1.6x for a very long time.  But, we started to fall behind on features, some of which are in MyBB 1.8x and having HF on the current branch was starting to look like a requirement more than an option.

One day I just said, "FUCK IT, LET's BREAK THIS SHIT" and so I did.  I knew that going to 1.8x would break many things and it most certainly did.  Luckily I am capable enough to fix just about anything but it takes time and energy to system administrate for this site.  I also of course have to offer support and run the sites day to day operations.  So things do take time for me to get things done.

After the upgrade I did my best to fix important stuff and we're actually pretty close to having HF not only fixed but improved.  One real serious issue during the upgrade was that the posts table didn't create that index and only until now do I know why.  I will explain in a minute.  Without the index search in posts was horrendous and I was forced to disable it because a query took 60 seconds and just a handful of people searching would explode the resources.  This made search unbearable and broke things like thread searching (that search box on the bottom of showthread).  I was not pleased but I knew the fix.  Unfortunately the fix would require me to take the site offline.

A few weeks ago I tried to fix the index but had continued problems running the query and after 3-4 hours I realized I needed a different approach. I waited a few days and tried something else and that also didn't work as planned.  We had minimal site downtime but this was getting annoying.  

I created a new plan of action.  Yesterday I enacted that.

I began by making backups and closing the site down.   My plan was to do a table copy.  I exported the structure, then created table mybb_posts2 and ran this:
INSERT INTO `mybb_posts2` SELECT * FROM `mybb_posts`;

Awesome, it was working.  Then...oh....then it went bad.  The partition which stores the MySQL data actually got full. Anyone that knows about unix systems is that you don't want to fill a partition.  So now I'm like "OH WTF".  I had taken the site offline to run this query and for 3 hours it ran.  Luckily HF wasn't broken but my 2nd attempt had once again FAILED miserably.  I was really unhappy about this and I wasn't going to stop this time so I went with my next option to fix the DB.

My last attempt was to do a data only table dump.  I'd TRUNCATE the table, add the index, and import the dump.  Sound easy doesn't it?  

Knowing my partition was full I had to move the data somewhere else on the server with more space.  Unfortunately it's a slower SATA drive and read/write IO is very important on things like this.   But I knew what I was doing and I was confident this would work.  I spent more time getting backups and preparing and by about 6pm my time yesterday I turned HF off and began the process once again to build the index by doing a full table import.  At about 2pm it was still running and about 70% done (running process shows percentage while working).  I went to bed figuring around 7-8am it would be done.  During a data import the index is automatically built and I should have been able to just turn HF on again.

Oh it never goes exactly as planned.  When I turned HF on the new posts weren't posting. Error logs showed that the pid column was not set as AUTO_INCREMENT.  And for HF to function properly that does need to be there. It is not an index per se but it's close. I looked at my MySQL STRUCTURE export which I imported for the table and I saw the code to set the pid column AUTO_INCREMENT but dammit...no good.  I went into the CLI (shell) for MySQL and ran the query I had.  

ALTER TABLE `mybb_posts` MODIFY `pid` `pid` INT(10) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT

Oh that looked just fine to me but guess what! Wrong sytax.  The MODIFY should have been CHANGE....ugh....so that's what went wrong and I suspect it's where it went wrong with the mybb_posts message column too.  Remember earlier I said I would explain later? Now is that later.  One simple word. An error unnoticed that caused havoc across the HF world.

Well, it was 8am and I had few choices. I was committed to getting this done and we were almost there.  

So I ran this:
ALTER TABLE `mybb_posts` CHANGE `pid` `pid` INT(10) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT

And the waiting began again. That query alone took 9 hours and 26 minutes to run.  Much of the day I was in XMPP with many members just updating them on the percentage and twiddling my thumbs. I did do other work like setup a VPS for the Wiki site, it's moving shortly.  But it was a gruesome wait because we started to come to 24 hours offline for this and that sucks.  I originally estimated 2-4 hours of downtime but I was far off.  

Eventually around 6pm the query finished.  And from there it was a breeze.   Everything was working great!  As expect the search was fixed, the database was running smooth and HF was online once again.  I did move the MySQL data folder back to the SSD as there was a noticeable speed difference from the SATA drive.  I'd say 1-2 seconds was added for each page load as well as slower searches.    I took backups, undid some my.cnf changes, and made sure that this time HF came online it stayed online.

Search is vastly improved now and we even have a minimum 3 characters again. I have it set for 500 results which should be fine.  More adjustment might be made as we go forward but overall everything is normal again and better than ever.

I can't say it went perfect. But it did get done.  

I am going to look into doing backups and recovery using different methods such as xtrabackup by Percona.  That can hopefully improve situations like this.  I'm a little bit worried about the MySQL data partition because it has about 15Gb space left.  Enough space for couple years of posts but not any space to do anything like we just did.  I can certainly manage it though and I plan to move our database again sometime this year to a server with more RAM.  The database total is now 30Gb but the indexes are another 25-30Gb by themselves.  

The work done in the past 24 hours was some of the most extensive work that needed to get done on HF which required downtime. We should be good after this for the minor changes HF will have and additional fixes.  With Xerotic and F8's help I will be able to get a lot more done in the coming months.

Expect more out of HF in the coming days and thank you for reading and waiting patiently.
subject: Downtime, Database, and Search Rejuvenation

message:
Xerotic and I have added a new plugin to HF that does a Post Editing History.

It's a plugin at MyBB which we've altered to suit HF.  It creates versions of the post and allows Admins and Staff to view editing history, to compare, and even revert.

We've also altered the plugin for some additional limitation settings.  

"Number of Edits Allowed"  - This is currently set to 10.  Which means once you've edited your post 10 times you will not be able to edit it again.

"Time Between Edits" - This means you must wait 30 seconds between your edits.  

Edits are not logged if done within an hour.  The edit history is pruned after 60 days. 

I'll try to explain how this all functions for you.

1. You make a post.
2. You must wait at least 30 seconds before you can edit.
3. If you want more than 1 hour to edit the post the version is stored in the history log.
4. If your post has 10 edits in the history log it will not allow you to further edit the page.
5. After 60 days edits are pruned so if you had 10 edits and 1 got pruned you can edit it again.

So to recap and explain again. You can't edit a post within 30 seconds.  Only after 1 hour of your last edit will a new edit be saved. You could potentially edit a new post 10 times in 30 minutes but only 1 edit is actually saved.  

I may alter the plugin further and adjust settings according to the communities needs but this should work well enough for us now.

This plugin now prevents all forms of edit abuse.

Any questions?

If you find a bug please report it to me asap.

message:
We must become mobile friendly.  This means the tabs must go.  We will never accomplish mobile friendliness with them.  The index navigation has to change and then so does forumdisplay and showthread pages.  This is not an option. It must happen.

This was Google's message in 2015:
https://support.google.com/adsense/answer/6196932?hl=en

[quote]Starting April 21, 2015, Google Search will be expanding its use of mobile-friendliness as a ranking signal. This change will affect mobile searches in all languages worldwide and will have a significant impact in Google Search results. Users will find it easier to get relevant, high quality search results optimized for their devices. [/quote]

Notice the "significant impact", well that's what HF is feeling.  It's imperative that we move to a mobile friendly design in order to return to the high quality results we once had.  We rank very high on all desktop results but get almost nothing for mobile devices.  This is a huge and immense problem that has to get resolved asap.   

Unfortunately vast change requires vast patience from members as well as understanding that new designs are required. Everyone loves the tabs.  The TABS MUST GO.  Just how it is.  You may not like other versions of HF without them and you may deem navigation awkward but this is not a choice anymore. It's something that has to be done.  

It angers me greatly that my attempts to push us to mobile friendly were not well recieved.  As a matter of fact many of you acted like complete assholes.  This is unacceptable.   I'm not sure what I have to say to get it through your heads.  You must understand these words...WE MUST BE MOBILE FRIENDLY.  

I'm not sure how or when I'm going to get the work done because right now everything is just crazy.  I'm still fixing a ton of stuff from the MyBB update and a decent part of that decision to do it was to prepare us for mobile friendliness.  A lot of 1.8x theme is already divs instead of tables, so that's helpful.  

Once HF is fixed up I will be planning a path for us to be mobile friendly.  I'll work on a theme in a dev environment and any live beta testing will be as a secondary theme choice and not default.  

But this has to happen.  Tabs will have to go. Things have to get done that many of you won't like but I hope the changes over time will make sense and you might even grow to like them.  I can't stress it enough that this is a non-choice situation.  Expect it to happen.

Thank you.

I'm going to add them to HF.  I honestly don't want to, but I know everyone expects them here.  Everyone wants them.  As much as it pains me to think of my site with them I have to at some point acknowledge it is what everyone else wants.  I have fought doing so for years because I don't believe in them and I want to run my site how I want to run it.  

The internet is changing.  It's always evolving and unless I find a way to update HF we risk dying as an old site with old tech.  And that's not what I want HF to be.  

https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=5674610

That thread did it for me.  A new member who simply just asked where notifications were.  As if it's an obvious feature that should be here but he just can't find.  

I want HF to be special but websites are becoming less and less unique imho.  It's also becoming harder to stand out.  I think people generally don't visit websites anymore.  They use apps and popular social media.  The days of finding a cool corner of the internet to hang out at are dwindling very fast.  

I'm doing my best to move HF in a new direction and that's starting with the API.  A lot more changes are coming even ones I have fought for years.  I'm going to remove a lot of irrelevant and semi-pointless rules.  Policies that were good 8 years ago don't make sense today.  Obviously I got rid of the RKO a week ago.  API v2 beta is going to be here next week.  Apps will follow and notifications are right in the mix.  

I'm trying to rethink HF as if I was starting fresh instead of just keeping this place managed day-to-day.  I keep wondering if it's time to move away from MyBB but that may seem drastic, still it's a thought I have.  I truly hope the API is going to do amazing things for the community.  It's definitely a step in the right direction.  

Anyways, this thread was originally about notifications so I'll end this rant on that topic.  I'll start to layout a plan for them and how to get them implemented properly on the site.  It's a big change for HF.  

Enjoy.

message:
Our email provider has made changes in the past few days that has caused great disruption to our email sending.  This effects registrations, notifications, and password resets.

I've been dealing with this since the 25th.  I've gone back and forth with them and today when I logged in the account was suspended.  Essentially they have altered their security triggers in a way that the HF account is flagged for potential abuse automatically.  

They know it's a false positive and quickly activated the account but the problem is they still have these triggers that may continue to falsely activate and suspend our email account. 

It's completely frustrating and I'm forced to make some hard decisions about how our email is delivered and what services I use.  I may end up dropping them after 4 years of solid email delivery service.  

I've taken their advice and made account alterations per their suggestions but at each turn it's only made things worse.  One of their last suggestions was that I use HTML formatting for emails.  So I took a couple more hours and altered all our outgoing emails to be HTML.  Also did some link formatting and changes so that the email were prettier.  I think it's crap because if plain text is a problem being flagged then I can't imagine HTML is better, but whatever, I'm doing everything they ask because I want this resolved asap.

They have an API which I already began coding functions into HF but apparently I have to do a lot more to really make this all efficient.  I'd like members to be able to check their own email status.

I've had a shitty ass weekend. Not going to lie.  Actually had a fairly crappy month but I'll just stick to the topic at hand.  

So to conclude:
1. I've had a shitty month.
2. Emails had disruptions over the past few days.
3. All outgoing emails are now in HTML format.

If anyone is experiencing problems with email delivery or formatting please contact me (PM please).  

If the issues can't get solved I may change email service providers or I may just setup my own VPS with an MTA and do this all myself.  Running your own MTA is a pain in the ass though simply because of potential spam filters and IP reputation problems.  

This is all rather annoying to deal with  just for something that should be simple.  

BLAH!

Flashpoint, a security company, has released on their blog a statement about the Mirai botnet and latest attack on DYN.  That attack took Krebs offline but then was directed at DYN which disrupted major companies like PayPal, Twitter, Reddit, GitHub, Amazon, Netflix, Spotify, and RuneScape.

[quote]Hackforums is a website mainly devoted to like-minded individuals who believe in learning new technical computer skills including security aspects. HF has very strict rules forbidding a variety of topics but at the same time we recognize that some topic discussion has to remain that could be used in a harmful manner. message:
For those wondering why they get slow HF loads or maybe just curious how HF is served...I made this new chart which represents most of how HF is served to you.

[img]http://hackforums.net/images/HF-served.gif[/img]

I'll try to explain the image and elaborate a bit.

We start at CF (Cloudflare) which has a WAF (Web Application Firewall) and a lot of rulesets.   Once we go through HF security we have Sucuri which again has DDOS protection and assists in grabbing traffic that CF doesn't block.  I don't always have Sucuri enabled as it tends to have a higher rate of false positives and their setup is sometimes buggy.  

Next we hit a server which has an OS kernel based firewall which I personally manage.  It's also a tunnel server.  Packets that hit this server are then tunneled to the next server which runs Nginx.

Nginx has some modules for DDOS protection.  Nginx serves all the static content. It then forwards any php requests to Apache.  You may wonder why I don't use Nginx to forward to Apache but I have my reasons.  I have some custom written modules for Apache that I can't replace with Nginx. These modules enhances HF security and ddos protection.  They are irreplaceable.  Once you pass Nginx though you do get forwarded to Apache which as I stated does have a lot of modules and is setup fairly well.  

Apache will forward the PHP calls to the PHP CGI processor.  That's when the nuts and bolts of the actual serving of the page truly begins.   PHP grabs the database (different server) information and serves your browser the page.

And so that's why HF doesn't load in .5 seconds and miraculously does load in just 2-3 seconds (most pages anyways).  

This setup has taken me years to mature into with layers being added as needed based on attacks, security requirements, technology changes, and the size of HF itself.

So when I get a PM saying a person is blocked or having slow page loads you must understand that it's not a 10 second (or even 10 minute) fix to figure out why one user is having a problem.  Each layer has protections which could slow you down or even block you.  

For those who doubt that we need all this....

[img]http://i.imgur.com/gJFCrxn.jpg[/img]

That's the past month.  It's nearly 3 BILLION requests and that's over 60 TB of traffic too.  And yet our downtime is for the most part minimal in comparison to the sizes of the attacks.  

Sometimes attacks are worse too.  Cloudflare just lets me display past month.  

And that's not everything either.  It's just what I'm willing to post about.  Do we go offline sometimes?  Yes, we do.  And I'm sure we'll continue to be attacked regularly.  I never honestly care about who is attacking or why they are.  My only concern is keeping HF online.  At this point there is a lot of automation built into protection.  Some protections are always enabled while others toggle on/off based on attack patterns.  And there is always things I can do manually.  

After the past 10 days of rather large attacks I went into a few of our layers and tightened them up.  We should see even better uptime now.  Doubt a day will ever come where we will see 100% uptime but I'm happy with even 98% considering the frequency of attacks.

Thank you.

I'll be honest about it and say that in the past I maybe was able to read only about 20% of all the contacts I get.  So many are completely stupid and weeding through to find the important ones was very tough and time consuming.

But a few weeks ago I've changed my email client and begun to streamline the contacts.  By using filters and pre-written canned responses I've now been able to respond to 100% of all contacts for the past 2 weeks. There is zero backlog right now.

That means accounts with lost Gauth get responses along with many more lost accounts recovered.  If you have a friend or are a temp account in need of recovery then you should use the contact form with option "Gauth/2FA Problem."  It's almost assured you'll get a response within 24 hours now, if not sooner.

The account recovery process is not guaranteed that you will get a recovery but now at least you'll get a response.  In most cases that do get recovery I will have a matching IP or at least a matching ISP/Region for me to disable Gauth.  A disabled Gauth may also mean you'll get an RKO.  That option is at my discretion.  I decide based on risk factors and the account history.

I'm doing all I can to give the best customer service.

Thank you.

message:
What a week this has been.  I've been working diligently to figure out what has been going on with the stolen accounts.  

This might be a good time to read the first notification again in case you've mistaken some of the rumors as facts.
http://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=5258345

It turns out we are NOT COMPROMISED. There is NO EXPLOIT. There is no DUMP or LEAK of the HF DB.

As it happens there was a code logic problem with my IP Login History plugin which I never noticed before.  MyBB uses the same hook name in two places which it should not do but it does.  So the plugin ran correctly with one hook and incorrectly on the second hook. That caused an IP to be logged incorrectly as logged into the account.  Gauth plugin actually interrupted the login process in a way that the second hook didn't run if 2FA was enabled on the account. Explains why no 2FA enabled accounts had the false logging.

A few lessons from this.

1. Don't believe all the trolls telling you that they hacked HF.
2. Don't allow anyone to blackmail, threaten, or extort you over your HF account.
3. I'll always work as hard and fast as I can to figure out the problem and to fix it.

I do feel like I have egg on my face.  All this drama was indeed my own doing.  I did my best to contain it but of course if indeed HF had been compromised it was important that members know.  

Pretty F'n funny that a small piece of code logic (bug) could cause so much drama.  I'm very happy to make this announcement.

I'd like to officially thank the one person who helped cause this fiasco. He's the guy who attempted logins into all these accounts.  Around the 4th day of my work I contacted what I hoped was a valid email address for him.  He responded that it wasn't an exploit and he was just trying to get an HF account to make some money.  He was a ban evader which I've been very successfully banning his new accounts.  He resorted to finding a way to steal active accounts.  In my communication with him he told me that he was using a simple method to obtain the accounts but it didn't make any sense to me at first.  He was possibly not the actual account thief, lying to me, or some other third option which I had not yet thought of.   

I headed out for a late-night drink after a long-day of work.  Upon return I had a clear and yet foggy head.  Then it came to me.  I realized how it could all fit.  I was almost certain of the problem causing this but it was very late and I needed to sleep on it.  Upon awaking I was still sure of my hypothesis and needed to hop onto the server asap.   Within minutes I had confirmed my deductions about the bug and spent the next hour fixing it.  Hallelujah!  We're fixed and not exploited or compromised.  :)

The person who pushed this bug and caused me much grief this week will get some type of bounty and likely a fresh Ub3r account along with some awards.  I hold no ill will towards him.  It's going to be up to him if he wishes the notoriety of these claims.  He was actually stealing some accounts but more like 5 not 50 and his method was completely users fault for using cross-site passwords. 

Some good things of course are how serious we all took account security and some measures were put into place to increase it. Also an important bug with logins is fixed.  

We no longer need a full site PW reset.  However, I do plan on implementing expiration dates for passwords with a 6 month rotation.   More on that feature later.

You may now exclaim your joy and relief.
subject: Account Security Saga Ends

message:
As part of our roadmap to enhance account security we will be doing a full site password reset for all accounts.  So everyone at some point in the near future will be getting an email to reset their password. If you do not get the email then you will lose access to your account.  

Please confirm your email is valid and accepting HF emails unfiltered.  If you need to change your account email please do so now. You will need to have a valid working email account that does not spam filter HF emails.

Use this link to check or change your email:
http://hackforums.net/usercp.php?action=email  (Only change your email if it's invalid such as lost access or doesn't get HF emails because of spam filters)

Also you will need to ensure that any notifications we send about changes will be allowed to be sent to you:
http://hackforums.net/usercp.php?action=options
Check the "Receive emails from the Administrators" please if you wish to get email notifications when we do send them. Please note we've only sent it out twice in nine years.  We have no intention to make it a habit of sending email blasts and we are against using email promotional spam.

I will ask that all members with 2FA/Gauth access enable it asap.  It's vital you secure your HF account using this method.
http://hackforums.net/gauth.php

If you have not done so also change your password even though we do plan on a reset it's good to have a fresh password on the site. One that you don't use anywhere else and is unique. Trust Scan page now shows when you last changed your PW. 
http://hackforums.net/usercp.php?action=password

I'm sure many will ask when we plan to do the password resets.  I can't say 100% for sure but my best guess is within two weeks.  Could be a lot sooner depends on how fast I work and what I find when it comes to the accounts security.  I may opt to upgrade us to MyBB 1.8x before doing a PW reset just in case there is an exploit being using in 1.6x series. In that case it could be a few weeks as it's a lot of work.  And it doesn't make sense to do a PW reset until I know we're secure.  

There are lots of rumors of dumps and leaks.  But let me make it clear that indeed these are rumors and there has yet to be any confirmation that indeed we have been dumped. I actually find it hard to believe since no one has shown actual proof they have the DB dumped.  Realize there are a lot of childish braggarts in this world.  Many will lie about having the DB when in-fact they don't have it.  Some will take credit for any compromise when in-fact they didn't do it.  Members are reporting being threatened or blackmailed, in which case, I suggest you ignore the bullies.  

If it wasn't for my own threads stating that I believe we've been compromised no one would be behaving any differently.  While I don't regret making the thread I do think it should be made clear that there is no actual proof so far.  I am starting to seriously question if we have been compromised in a way that a dump was possible.  Currently the situation is that we have Ub3r and l33t accounts being stolen.  No data on HF has been changed. The site is operating normally.  There has been no manipulation of the database as far as I can tell.  I've not found any shells on our servers.  I have not found any evidence at all that we're potentially compromised at any level beyond these stolen, or possibly sold, accounts.  

Normally in the past when we are indeed compromised it's much more evident.  The site is defaced. The database is leaked and I see actual proof.  Server gets owned with things like a root password change. Admin accounts get altered.  All types of mayhem normally occurs.  And the hackers delight in it, take credit, and do a full-on victory dance.  So far....nothing...and that's very odd.

These facts are very true:
1. I'll secure HF. 
2. I will secure accounts. 
3. HF will continue as usual. 
4. Eventually, we'll get compromised again. 
5. Rinse and repeat as they say.

Thank you.

message:
I can't say when or how but apparently somewhere at some point we had a compromise of account security.  It has to be based on my findings today.  

While conducting my normal day of checking for stolen accounts I came across a dozen or so Ub3r accounts stolen in the last few days.  Upon further inspection and looking for more accounts stolen or sold related to these accounts I found something rather alarming.  In my logs I found that nearly 40 accounts had attempts to login and it became obvious these were not sold accounts. Indeed these appear stolen.  I conclude that because out of the 40 accounts only the ones without 2FA were actually logged into and stolen.  And more than a few members of these stolen accounts closed have contacting me to claim they were not sold and their computers are not infected. 

That leads me to believe this person has the password of the account. They can only get that either by the member using the same password on another site, being infected by a RAT/keylogger, or if their hashed password was cracked from a dump.   So it's rather alarming to find this out.  

I have to conclude this was on our old hardware or some fluke compromise at some point when I was working on something. Could even have been MyBB vulnerability which is likely now patched.  If there was some way for the person to still have DB access I would assume they'd alter the member login or other site details and have their way.  Even do a complete dump (I have measures in place to make that very very difficult) which does not appear to have happened.  They'd also disable 2FA if they had SQL access and steal any account they wished.  

All accounts compromised are older than 1 year ago. Which might be when the compromise occurred, maybe. 

I am going to add a plugin which will now require 2FA to post in the Marketplace or to send a PM if you have an upgraded account with 2FA/Gauth access.  I have also altered the setting for the minimum character length of a password from 10 to 12 characters.  In the future that should slow down any decrypting of hashed passwords in case of a dump.

If there is a silver lining in this it's that we now know that 2FA works to secure accounts.  

I have contacted all the accounts compromised with 2FA enable and still open instructing them to immediately change their passwords and leave 2FA enabled.

Still, questions remain. When did it happen?  How did it happen?  Are we still insecure?  And unfortunately at the time of this writing I can't say.  I am still investigating this and messages have been sent to the members involved. With their help I should be able to get some answers to the previous questions.

I will need all members to change their passwords immediately and enable 2FA if you have an account with access.

Oh....btw some good news also...HF database does not store any private order data like name, address, or phone.  We only have the most basic info which is IPs and emails.  

It's very important for all members to check Trust Scan before making any deals.  The information provided on the page is plenty and should be enough to give you an indication of how secure the account has been and if it has behavior that would deem them a high risk.

An email is being sent to all Ub3r instructing them to create a new password and to enable Gauth/2FA.

This will give everyone something to talk about at the very least.

subject: Injuries and Losing My Mind

message:
You're a highway patrolman.  Your job is to make sure the roads are safe and that the rules of the road are followed.  So you sit on the side of the highway watching as cars go by.  When you see someone speeding you give them a ticket.  Sometimes you just do loops on the highway looking for activity like weird lane changes or eratic driving that might indicate a drunk driver.  And so, you see people get pulled over by the cops and mostly getting tickets and sometimes a cop pulls someone over in a stolen car or maybe they posses drugs and they are arrested and removed from the highway.

Now how well do you think the cop could do his job if he was called by the other drivers everytime one of them complained someone was speeding or driving like an a-hole.  And yes, you can actually call the police to inform them of such behavior, you can even take down the license plate so that police can find them easier.  But how often has anyone here ever seen anyone do that?  And let's say the cop finds the car and what happens if the car isn't speeding at the time they see it?  Do they have probable cause to pull you over?  Unlikely, simply based on a random tip by a stranger that doesn't have a radar gun and wouldn't be able to testify in court.  

Let's say you're driving now and you see a speeder going 110mph and nearly kills you in a bad maneuver.  Do you pull over to the next highway patrolman and bitch them out for not doing their job? Do you tell them they allow speeding?  He probably writes dozens of tickets a day that you'll never know about.  It's practically an invisible and thankless task.

So what is the job of the highway patrolman?  To sit on the side of the road and make sure people slow down when he's seen.  He catches speeders and tickets them. Sometimes he finds drunk drivers and might save a life by arresting them.  But most of the time he's just riding around making his presence known in order to create a sense of law and order so the decent people of the world can feel safer.  

Ultimately though we drive on the highway and it's up the the citizens to drive responsibly and to keep a good eye on the road for those bad drivers.  You cannot blame highway patrol when accidents happen or even if lives are lost.   They are just doing their job as best they can and following the guidelines given to them known by everyone on the highway.  Those that don't follow the rules often get away with it.  It's just how it is.  

And yes, this story is about me being the highway patrolman of HF and constantly being told I do nothing about scammers meanwhile I spend hours a day reviewing and closing accounts of members who indeed are scammers or intend to scam.  Getting rather fed up with that perception too.

Members must understand that I am NOT going to get involved in your deals or deal disputes.   I will not.  Scammers get banned CONSTANTLY.  Every day I close their accounts. [quote]
Lost or Stolen Account Policy
=========================

Any non-upgraded account reported as stolen or lost may be closed permanently by administration.  After it's closed as long as there are no Deal Disputes threads, scammer reputations, or Deal Dispute Database entries against the account you may open a new account.  The old account will be marked as "reported lost/stolen".

If any account is stolen or lost and then has Deal Disputes threads, scammer reputations, or Deal Dispute Database entries against the account it will be closed and marked as "lost/stolen scammer" and you will not be allowed to return to the community under any condition.  

If an upgraded account has 2FA enabled (GAUTH) and is stolen or lost and reported before any Deal Disputes threads, scammer reputations, or Deal Dispute Database entries  are placed against the account, the account will be banned as "Possibly stolen, lost, or compromised." Pending an investigation the account may be recovered to the original owner provided enough evidence of the accounts original ownership.

All account reported lost or stolen are subject to a Rep Kill.  If you lost your credentials you are irresponsible. If your account was stolen you are not security minded.  In either case we're going to RKO your account. 

All upgraded accounts now have full access to our Gauth (2-factor authentication) account security feature.  It is highly advised you enable it.  On the Gauth page are instructions to backup your security key in case of a lost, stole, or reset device.  It's vital you have a backup method because we will not guarantee account recovery.  Gauth enables you to secure your account and the burden is on you to maintain your own account security.

Account recovery is at the discretion of the Administration and there are no guarantees an account will be recovered.

So it's clear to everyone, HF accounts cannot be shared, transfered, or sold.  Any evidence we have that gives us the impression an account is no longer in full possession of the original account owner is subject to being closed.  

We reserve the right to close any account for any reason at any time.

I'm going to try a new approach in dealing with reputation abuse.  

I've altered the [url=http://hackforums.net/misc.php?action=help&hid=20]Rep Help Doc[/url].

The following is either new or changed:

What is reputation abuse?
• Scammer Reputation: You're required to leave a link to a Deal Dispute thread you have created to infer someone is a scammer (ie: scammer, scams, chargebacks, scamming). Please note that a Deal Dispute link must be your own thread you've created. It cannot be a thread opened by another member.
 • Deal Dispute Linking: We don't allow you to link to a Deal Dispute forum thread that's opened by another member.
 
 
 Can members write anything they want when giving reputation?
 No. Our forum has a no flaming policy, and this also applies to reputations. If a member is seen flaming, they will receive a warning from staff. Also, a reputation accusing someone of being a scammer must be followed with a link to the scam report thread that you have made. Please note that there is a fine line between rude and crude and we consider very crude language to be a violation while rude language might be allowed. When you get a negative rep it's likely going to say something you don't agree with or like. We suggest you don't take it personal as all members get these type of reputations eventually.
 
 
 How do I report an invalid scammer reputation?
 We suggest you send them a Private Message informing them of site policy and the consequences unless they alter the reputation within 24 hours. Give them that time to alter it. Do not report the reputation to an admin until that 24 hours has passed. Do not threaten the member in the PM. Instead copy/paste this:

[b] I am sending this PM to you because you've given me an invalid scammer reputation. Policy dictates that I send this text to you. HackForums policy requires that all scammer inferences in reputation require a link to a Deal Dispute forum thread that you have created. Either you didn't leave a link or the link you did leave is to a thread not created by you. As such you have 24 hours to alter your reputation to be within policy. Failure to do so will result in your reputation being reported to an admin which can result in severe action against your account. If you'd like to confirm this policy please read this help doc:
 http://hackforums.net/misc.php?action=help&hid=20[/b]


I really hope these help minimize abuse here and lowers the amount of reports I get.

Here is what got done:

Upgrade FreeBSD (major version)
Reinstall Named (destroyed during in upgrade)
Fixed server kernel based firewall
Install two GCC versions (took over 2 hours to build them, GCC sucks to build)
Rebuild FTP
Rebuild PHP
Rebuild Apache

This was like starting a server from scratch.  Not fun. All I wanted to do today was optimize the database. Then I figured I would upgrade MariaDB. Then I found out it required FreeBSD 10+ because of a library.  Then after I install the major version upgrade everything just feel apart. Which I should have expected I guess.  

This is the worst part. A bug in the build for MariaDB 10.1 on FreeBSD 10+ exists. 
https://mariadb.atlassian.net/browse/MDEV-8973

So honestly the reason we were down for all those hours was to try and upgrade our Maria install.  Which in the end I didn't even accomplish. I'm rather pissed off about that. At least we got upgraded on FreeBSD but realistically not that great of an accomplishment.

Sorry to everyone for another handful of hours of downtime we had to all endure.  With the server move, updates, optimizing, upgrades, attacks, and even datacenter outages it's been a rather heavy workload. And I still have so much more to do too.  Now you know why I took so long to start this process.  It's likely to continue for a couple  more months like this too because I'm fairly sure the MyBB upgrade will be the most difficult process of all. Ugh.

I fear we have more downtime coming too.

message:
I'm going to need to run a nearly two hour query to optimize our database search function.  I prefer to get it done right now because I'm not going to stay up till 3am doing it in the middle of the night.  

I keep making adjustments and optimizations to our database and likely this is one of the final actions I'll need to take that will create this much downtime.  

Basically the InnoDB default search stopwords is total crap.  It's very minimal and for a forum our size it needs to be a lot more robust. The stopwords are words that the index ignores. Words like "hello" or "the" which not only are pointless to search but pointless to index.  The index takes a LOT of resources in both CPU and RAM.  So making sure it's optimal is very important.    Default max word is also 84 characters which is very long. I'm lowering it to 64 which is still very long but should suit our needs. Long enough to also index crypto txn's too.

I want to get this done before we move to MyBB 1.8x. The more I can optimize the database the better the upgrade should go.

So expect a Site Closed message within the next 30 minutes and sorry for more downtime but this is just part of such a large structural change to the site.

Thanks.

message:
We are now on MariaDB.  I made the decision to go with MariaDB after reviewing the performance of MySQL 5.6 since moving to the new servers.  It was reasonable but CPU imho was a bit high.  I knew I could always move to MariaDB and I decided two days ago to perform the move today and see how it goes.

I also did a lot of research and reading about MariaDB. Not a lot of the features we'll use and MyBB doesn't have any extra compatibility. But the fact that MariaDB is a drop-in replacement might end with MariaDB 11.  I read that from the actual MariaDB dev team.  So with that in mind I decided to make the adjustment now instead of waiting till I was required to make a more complicated upgrade.

So far the CPU went from a near 100% of a single CPU cycle to only 5% or less. That's incredibly significant in terms of performance.  Overall server load has gone from 60-70% CPU idle to 85-90% CPU idle.  This gives us a lot more room when it comes to CPU cycles and what freedom I have to add features to HF.  There does seem to be extra RAM used but fortunately we have plenty of that on the DB server.

The next maintenance upgrade will be to Nginx for some additional DDOS protection features I plan to implement.

Thanks to all members for being patient while I performed the upgrade.  Much appreciated. Enjoy.

message:
Just a heads up that I spent most of my time this week finishing up the new server. I expected to be moved already but time hasn't allowed it.  The work I did was mainly security and making sure it has all the features and services I need.  There are still a couple modules I plan to add to Nginx but after that it will be 100% production ready and I'll move the site.

Once we're moved I'll upgrade MyBB to 1.8x branch and that's when the shit will hit the fan.  We'll see how well it goes but I expect a buttload of problems.  Plugins will break and I'll have to build a new theme.

As for new theme. I have what many might consider good news. I'm going to try and recreate our old theme (Black Reign).  We'll also revert to the old userbars for the official groups.  

I wanted to keep most of this a surprise but I figured some of you are anxious for some changes around here.  I am as well.  

The new setup is definitely going to allow us a lot more options when it comes to resources.  Options and features I wouldn't dare consider on our current servers should be no problem on the new setup.

One major change will be search, which is totally broken and hardly functions.  MySQL 5.5x added good InnoDB support but it doesn't have full-text search which means I had to move to a separate solution for search and we use a Sphinx plugin.  It functions but when MyBB added prefixes they didn't work. Also some other problems with cache and some searches just don't work well.  The plugin is very out of date.

MySQL 5.6x which will be used on the new DB server does support InnoDB full-text search.
http://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.6/en/fulltext-restrictions.html

I know it will be a resource hog but I'm praying that the new specs on the DB server will be more than enough.  We'll find out once we move and I'll make adjustments as best I can.  

Another major change will be that we'll run Nginx in-front of Apache.  This will give me much greater control over serving and blocking layer-7 DDOS attacks.  We'll still run behind Cloudlfare but this change will add yet another layer to our protection.  So far my testing has been excellent and how I have the server setup, as complex as it is, seems to be doing very well. We won't really know this until we're production and site is actually running on the setup.

I'm also 90% done with the pages for automated sticky purchasing.  I wanted to complete it but I'm actually having some difficulty with some logic on my code.  Mainly to ensure I don't oversell and that the invoice for a new sticky is properly done.  Otherwise most of the code and front-end is written.  Very close to completing it.  I go back and forth between working on it and also working on the server setup.

I'm sorry we haven't moved yet.  I'll be honest.  I'm a but hesitant because I know the workload will be tremendous the second I move the site.  It won't just take me days to get us 100%, it will take me months and the first week or two will be hectic. So I've more or less just waited for better timing to make sure I have at least 5-7 days of open time to do it all. 

I'm looking at doing the move on a Monday-Wednesday when the site is less busy.  Can't be sure if this will happen this week or I'll wait till next.  

On a side note: I'm becoming very frustrated with scammer rep abuse.  I don't want this thread to devolve in a discussion on the topic but let's just say things need to change around here.  The only reason I mention it is because it's on my mind constantly and I feel like I can't make serious changes until this server move happens.  But I want to give notice that things will change and they won't continue to be as they are. I consider the reputation problem a top priority.

I guess that's all I have to say about the matter for now.  

Thanks and stay tuned.

message:
We get so many idiot rumors about our DB being leaked and passwords hacked.  99% of the time it's bullshit.  

There was one user table dump in 2011.  The Witza orders DB was dumped in 2012.  

That's it. In 8 years that's our 2 biggest compromises. 

The user table dump was easily fixed and correct a long long time ago.  It's a near harmless dump now except for spammers using the emails which most are probably dead now.

The order DB did not compromise any accounts. Instead it did create problems for members being blackmailed, dox'd, and swatted.  Unfortunately not much I can do about it.  Measures were put into place to prevent a recurrence if our DB was compromised again by chance.  

Yet, ever few months some idiot "leaks" our DB and pretends it's new.  Some even try to sell it. It's an obvious scam or a troll.

I do look into these accusations and any evidence that by some chance it's true.  We're not compromised.  It's not true.

Be aware even if we were we require strict passwords of 10 character length with digits, uppercase, and lowercase. Very hard to crack.  

I also have triggers setup that would definitely tell me if the DB was dumped.  I have lots of security measures in place and while no website is 100% secure. Let it be known we're not an easy target and that after all these years it's really only one time my self-managed servers were compromised and that was very briefly.   I don't think that's too bad for 8 years. The rest of our instances of nonsense were simple SE to companies we uses services from for serving HF.  

So don't freak out at every thread you see on the web about rumors we're hacked. Ask for evidence.  If they can't provide it then it didn't happen.   I'd say at least once every 2 weeks I get some panicked noob sending me a screenshot which happens to be from the 2 dumps I mentioned.  

Thanks.

Note: Point your noob friends on Skype telling you HF is hacked to this thread. Shut them up.

message:
A couple months ago I rented a new server for us and I've slowly been working on it as the time has presented itself.

Given how much BS we're dealing with lately I'm trying to push up the timetable to accomplish a full server move.  

Our existing servers are old.  They are underpowered and don't have enough resources.  Certain options which I'd love to add to HF I have not been able to do.

The new servers are amazing.  The DB server alone has 96GB of ram and 24 cores.  More than enough power and room to implement new features and to run HF for at least 5 more years. 

The HTTP server is right now running both Nginx and Apache with Nginx as the reverse-proxy.  I just got done setting it up to my satisfaction.  I have a lot of special needs and custom stuff I run.  It's running like a charm right now.

Things that will improve after the move:
1. Load time.  Already quick but should be even faster.
2. Search.  I should be able to ditch Sphinx search in favor of the built in InnoDB FT searching. Biggest difference will be that I can likely set min characters to just 3 and that results will be more accurate.  We should also have searching by Thread Prefix working too. That's going to open up some possibilities for plugins or custom changes.
3. Notifications.  Yes, I might, just might consider options.
4. Uptime.  The new setup should in theory provide us with a lot better uptime.  The NGINX reverse-proxy provides me a new tool to stop certain attacks that have been hounding HF.
5. Security.  The new servers have a few extra security measures I've placed.  Can't really elaborate but the servers do have a deeper setup than existing ones.

I am sure there is more too. Many suggestions are rejected just based on resources.

I still need to continue working and doing more testing.  I am almost certainly going to upgrade us to the latest branch of MyBB 1.8x.  That itself is going drive me crazy with changes to plugins and templates.

Once we're on 1.8 I'm going to work on making our template a responsive design.  Hopefully I won't have too much trouble and we can look forward to a truly good site experience for mobile and desktop users alike.

So that's an update to what's going on and how I spent the last 24 hours.  It's going to be a big summer around here.  Changes are coming and all of them are improvements.  

Thank you for reading.

message:
Going to have to discuss this openly to members.

Cloudflare has an exploit that's being used to bypass their security. It's related basically to CNAME DNS entries.  Basically anyone can setup a cname pointing to HF then attack that cname entry and it will 100% bypass the Cloudflare protection scheme. It's fucked up.  It's really fucked up.

I knew about this exploit months ago and reported it to them.  At the time they basically dismissed it.  I removed any cnames in my own account that I knew were being used to attack HF and it resolved the issue. Then about 2 weeks ago we had the weekend with 2 days of extended downtime. I was actually offline spending time with family.  

I sent ticket after ticket to Cloudflare and they were basically clueless and the support person I initially had was a moron.  Eventually they bumped up my ticket to higher tech and they stopped the attack. At least it appeared that way.

Over the course of the past 2 weeks the CNAME exploit has repeatedly been used as I believe it's now a little more well-known and actively being used as a Cloudflare bypass in DDOS attacks.  This has become a real problem of course as unfortunately over time I've changed my protection scheme so much that I rely in-part with Cloudflare.

Because Cloudflare is a reverse proxy setup the traffic hitting my server requires DPI (Deep Packet Inspection) for the attacking IPs to be stopped at the server firewall level.  Otherwise it goes to Apache which even if blocked by Apache still gobbles up resources and chokes the service thus making the denial of service complete.  This is what has been happening.

Possible combats to this would be to install some sort of DPI alteration to my server firewall.  Possible to do but annoying as fuck and very resource (CPU) intense. It's not optimal. My other option is NGINX reverse proxy which doesn't choke and would likely work to stop the types of attacks that have recently occurred.  Last option was to double up the protection that Cloudflare offers by using another reverse proxy and WAF setup such as Sucuri.net.

Yesterday attacks resumed taking us offline once again.  Another support ticket with Cloudflare was opened.  I let them know point blank about the CNAME exploit and I was offline.  Hours passed and still no results.  

The problem with successful DDOS attacks against HF is that they just embolden attacks, word spreads, and even more attacks occur.  So my main objective when HF is under attack is fast and efficient mitigation.  Thwarting attacks is a high priority for me. I not only want the uptime but I also want to show attackers that their efforts are wasted.  Our uptime has greatly improved because of that.

Back to Cloudflare...so the attack last night persisted. The support ticket was becoming frustrating.  A change was required in order to deal with this.  The fastest change I could immediately come up with was Sucuri.  So that's what I did. At 10pm last night I paid for a new account, changed server configurations, and began the necessary changes to add their protection into our serving scheme.  

So far it's been a reasonable success with a few problems. I think we're going to lose NSFW mode. At least in it's current form.  

Sucuri allows me to block countries not just challenge them as Cloudflare does. That means a lot of users are 100% blocked.  For now the listed allowed countries is relatively small and I'm sure adjustments will be made.

We still run through Cloudflare for now.  I can't be 100% sure I will continue to use them or if I'll downgrade my Business account to just Pro. I'm pretty frustrated that for nearly two weeks they haven't fixed this problem and I'm guaranteed 100% uptime. Even worse is their inept responses to me in support tickets.  I've lost faith in their service and that's an understatement.

Going forward I may or may not run both services. I may drop the Business CF account into a simple Pro account.  I was already planning on a major change to our servers this summer which may include running Nginx on port 80 and reverse-proxy to Apache.  Some wonder why I still run Apache and that's because it does have some very useful modules I use including a couple custom ones I wrote.  I just don't have the time or patience to deal with the same type of setup with Nginx.  But running it as a reverse-proxy should allow me even more control and another layer of protection.

I've had a sleepless night and hoping to do all I can today to get things working as best as possible but changes will occur and odd behaviors will happen.  Feel free to report them to me either directly or through PM.  I'm likely going to be agitated all day over this. I'm less than pleased at Cloudflare and so far I can already see limitations and problems with Sucuri.  

On a final note: Many of you have been reporting to me incorrectly the exploit and what you deem as fixes.  Most of these reports don't understand the attack (skids).  Many of those don't understand that I already block the traffic at the service level but Apache SUCKS and if you have 5000 IPs coming in it will choke hardcore despite my efforts. And without DPI at the server firewall level the traffic can't be stopped.  This was a complete failure of Cloudflare whose protection scheme I've paid for and failed.  I put that downtime on them.  I made them aware of the problem months ago.  Before 99% of those using the exploit even knew it existed.  

Thanks to everyone who has assisted and supported HF.  Let's hope our uptime gets to 99.9%.

[sp]Fuck sleep. Coffee day[/sp]

message:
This is something that has always bothered me when it comes to security and MyBB.  

Let's say you have 2 or even 3 devices logged into HF.  And on one device you logout.  The cookies on the other devices will remain logged in.  Yes, that's convenient but it's also a partial security risk.  When I log out I expect all sessions to delete.

So in an effort to increase security, even if just a tiny bit, from now on when you click the logout link all sessions will be destroyed and all devices will require a login.  

That's not to say you can only be logged into one device at a time.  You can login to 10 devices if you want but just one logout and they will all need to login again.

Hope this helps. Enjoy and thanks.

Seems like someone is using the 2010 dump to bruteforce logins.  

Back then a user table dump occurred and I was forced to close inactive accounts and force password changes on all upgraded members.
