My main concern at that time was securing upgraded accounts.  Which we did.  Took about a month to recover all the accounts that were stolen.

Back then we didn't require complex passwords and too many clowns used simple passwords like "password" and no, I'm not joking.

That dump floats around even today but it's value is nearly zero.  Someone apparently took the time to unhash a buttload of account credentials and then bot the login page for the past few hours.  

All they managed to do was make my evening interesting and I was able to tidy up the problem rather easily.  They were able login to less than 100 open registered accounts which are all now closed.  Only 2 inactive L33t accounts were stolen and those are closed now too. Not one Ub3r account was compromised.

Of course I took care of the bot as well.  That won't be able to continue either. 

I'm just letting members know your accounts are secured. There was some obvious weird online list with closed accounts which of course alerted us all. Thanks to those who brought it to my attention.

Silly skids...bruteforcing is for noobs.

message:
I've just completed and published a Help Doc for the XMPP service.
http://hackforums.net/misc.php?action=help&hid=39

Basically it's the foundation of policies as well as helpful info for users on privacy.

To highlight a few things:


1.  Server runs Prosody for XMPP server software and it's written in Lua.  http://prosody.im/

2. We are logging IP's and timestamps to ensure integrity and dissuade abuse of the system.  

3. Messages are not logged. 

4. We require OTR to ensure that even if messages are logged they would look like this:

[quote]18:01:06 RECV: omniscient@hackforums.im: ?OTR:.
18:01:27 SEND: omniscient@hackforums.im: ?OTR:.
18:01:29 SEND: omniscient@hackforums.im: ?OTR:.
[/quote]

5.  You can't share your XMPP. Anyone caught sharing will get a closed HF and XMPP account. You're placing members at risk of being scammed or compromised and I won't tolerate that.   

Now I know many are questioning the integrity and security of the service.  HF IM XMPP is optional. It's a feature I've added to the site for upgraded members as a benefit. You are not required to use it. If you already use an XMPP service you like or maybe you simply prefer Skype then that's up to you.  

I've done my best to secure the server.  It's technically completely clean from being used to compromise HF.  The server could be rooted and there would be no compromise to HF itself. However knowing members are concerned about intercepted messages I've opted to removed Escrow's access to the server even as an XMPP admin. That means I'm the only guy with access to the server.  I've double checked logs and server security as best I can and I can say with confidence that we're secured. 

And while the server is definitely going to experience downtimes from attacks or other hiccups I remain confident that this service will be a long term feature for upgraded members that is widely used for a variety of reasons.

There will be continued work to integrate the HF IM XMPP service onto the site via profiles and easy to use links.  Unfortunately for now I'm shelving the idea of group chats or conference rooms.  

Thanks.

message:
The HF IM XMPP I'm declaring to be officially out of beta and released for all Ub3r group members.

Ub3r members can create and control their accounts here: http://hackforums.net/hfim.php

The rest is on the HF IM page and should all be pretty easy to use.

xadamxk has a very informative thread here: http://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=4547989

Here is some important troubleshooting issues we've come across:

[b][color=#FF0000]SSL Handshake error[/color][/b] - Upgrade your Pidgin client. If not using Pidgin then your client requires TLS v1.1+ support.

[b][color=#FF0000]Policy Violation[/color][/b] - You're already logged in on one device. We don't allow multiple device login for security purposes.

[b][color=#FF0000]Not Authorized[/color][/b] - Incorrect username/password which means double check your credentials and if still not working do a password change on the HF IM page.

[b][color=#FF0000]Remote connection closed[/color][/b] - Your router, firewall, or ISP may be blocking the port.  We're looking into possible solutions.  Also note we have our own firewalls that will block repeated login attempts so be careful you don't trigger those as well.

message:
This is actually something I've done to help with our XMPP but it can also be used to ask a member to verify themselves in other situations too.  

http://hackforums.net/verifysecret.php

It's linked from the Extra page as well.

It makes the most sense to use it with XMPP.  When you're in a session you can "authenticate" a buddy in a few ways. 

https://otr.cypherpunks.ca/help/4.0.0/authenticate.php

The XMPP will REQUIRE OTR to work.  And then if members using it also want to authenticate I have a simpler and more efficient way than sending PMs.  

1. Go to the Verify Secret page.  
2. Just enter the users UID which is part of their UID@hackforums.im account in the XMPP chat session.
3. Click the "Unverified" link in bottom right of the chat window.  You'll get options to authenticate and choose "Shared secret".
[sp][img]https://otr.cypherpunks.ca/help/4.0.0/auth-ss.png[/img][/sp]
4. Enter the secret you should have gotten on the Verify Secret HF page.  

You should now be verified and in a private HF IM XMPP chat with the user.  

A new secret is generated each day. That's not to say every 24 hours.  It's based on server time so that on Monday the server will generate a different secret than on Sunday.  Even if 15 minutes ago it passed midnight.  This is to prevent old secrets being reused or stolen.  You should verify each time you're in a chat if you want to be 100% sure you're speaking to the person from HF.

Be aware that by sharing your daily secret code openly to others may expose you to be impersonated.  In the XMPP client the other user does not see the secret. You just ask them to verify it.  You do not want to post it, pm it, or share it if you want it to be fully secure.  

You can safely use this also for other XMPP services using OTR.  It will work exactly the same.

Enjoy everyone.

https://www.openssl.org/~bodo/ssl-poodle.pdf

Some of you might be paying attention to these rather publicized exploits but some may not.  In either case the latest exploit bug in SSL was released about a week ago and labeled "Poodle" which stands for "Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption".  

It's basically a MITM exploit. Not really easy to take advantage of but considering this is now the 2nd time a huge SSL exploit was published I just wonder why members still send me requests for us to add SSL.  

It's imho very dangerous to falsely assume your safe because your browser has a little lock icon.  You should be relying on your own knowledge and your own connection for your own security. 

We may one day add SSL/TLS to the site.  Not sure when if ever but it might come. I just don't see why members are pushing for it at a time when SSL has been cracked twice.  And I've not once had an account stolen via MITM.  

We're more in need of other security options for accounts beyond an SSL connection like 2FA.  Which I am currently working on.

Thanks everyone and enjoy.

 If you're inactive your account is subject to being closed. If you've made posts the account will not be deleted. If you're not upgraded into L33t or Ub3r the account will not be recovered for any reason. Upgraded accounts can be reopened only under certain circumstances and with diligent evidence the account is yours. We expect 100% matching IPs, emails, and upgrade order information. Regular member accounts can be closed after 6 months inactivity. Inactive L33t and Ub3r are subject to closure after one year. The activity is based on account login. You are not required to post. 

Why do you close accounts?
 Accounts are closed to prevent old accounts being stolen or sold then used to abuse the community. 

What if my account is closed from being inactive and I want to participate at HF?
 If your account closure is from inactivity you can safely rejoin HF. However you should confirm with staff via the contact form that indeed your previous account was closed from inactivity. If before your closure you were banned it's likely we've closed your account for other reasons.[/quote]

message:
The irony of it all. I do all that database maintenance just a few days ago and on a day I was offline all day I come home to find the site offline.  This was unusual as my normal triggers didn't give me any indication that I was offline. So this was rather strange.

Trying to login to the backend of the database server was giving me a very strange error.  Without trying to go into a panic I began my work.  

I did a server power cycle. After 5-8 minutes of bootup I was in.  YES!  After a peek at the MySQL process it became obvious what happened.  We had a swapzone memory issue and the server collapsed due to memory being full.  That's not good but it's fixable.  

Another server power cycle reboot along with some recovery lines added to MySQL did their work and the process started.  MySQL has an InnoDB recovery mode which I used.  Worked perfect to fix what appeared to be the immediate issue.

A few tweaks and we're back online. Overall downtime appears to be about 14 hours.  I sincerely apologize.  The irony is that I just spent time with database maintenance.  I should have done a MySQL restart because I believe the many large actions I committed just used memory and it never cleared.  I do know we're reaching some limits.  I will definitely be putting priority into some hardware upgrading in the near future.

For those wondering where I was.  I was on Lake Mead with friends and family on a boat.  I was out there having a wonderful day and even did some water skiing.  Just so unfortunate that it seems so many times when I'm away that HF goes haywire.  I sincerely apologies to the members. For those with paid stickies that expired today I will allow you to keep them for another day.

Hope everyone has a good weekend.

btw...this was not related to any attack or exploit. Always some jokers that take credit if any HF downtime occurs. There has been no compromise to servers or data.

Thanks guys.

message:
Just wanted to point out a perfect example of how I deal with scammers on a daily basis and while I do not get involved in deal disputes I am always very very active in getting rid of ban evading scammers.

Certain patterns exist for scammers.

1. They use proxies or VPNs when possible.
2. Often purchase existing l33t/ub3r HF accounts.
3. They ban evade after they have previously scammed on account and reps are given.

What most scammers don't do...is continue to scam from the same account once they are left valid scammer reps.  

This is in the Reputations help docs:

[quote]How do I report abuse or get the invalid rep removed?
 You can PM the admin Omniscient. Be warned. If you did not read fully this page and the rep left on your account was indeed within policy then you will get RepFucked without any hesitation. If you were left a scammer rep we may also do a full investigation of your account. If we find out you're breaking any site policies you will get a closed account.[/quote]

Now believe it or not it's fairly common for ban evading scammers to report rep abuse to me.  And I finally added that wording above so they are aware I'm going to investigate their accounts of any scammer complaints or other policy violations.  

Members should note that also these accounts are CLOSED so you may not see them in the ban list or have any awareness that a scammer was just caught.  I do everything behind the scenes very low-key.

So here is the latest example of a member who contacted me about scammer rep abuse:
http://hackforums.net/member.php?action=profile&uid=2163119 (was l33t)
 
He sent me a PM and checking his rep he did indeed have an invalid scammer rep but as per my normal procedures I took a moment to review his account...which led me to this:
http://hackforums.net/member.php?action=profile&uid=2118296

Obvious multi accounter which a previous l33t account with valid negative scammer reputations. Only one conclusion to draw...ban evading scammer and BOTH accounts closed.  I could probably dig deeper and potentially find more accounts too.  Likely they are abandoned though and worthless.

But this should highlight an example of what I'm spending a lot of time on and I don't really talk about it.  There is a misconception that we don't ban scammers when in fact I do it every single day.  What I won't do is get involved in deals or deal disputes. 

 I can't talk about certain additional measures we have in place or what action I take because what I do is still working to catch many ban evading scammers. Now you know what's really going on...at least some of it. :)

Thanks.

Today is April 1, otherwise known as, April Fools Day.  It's a day when many across the world pull off harmless pranks for the lulz.  HF has had a tradition of using this day for some humor and pulling a prank or two on members.  

For 2014 April Fools we added a message to header that your account might be compromised and your posting privileges are suspended. A link to an account recovery page is available.  Your account is not compromised and the link is a fake Cloudflare loading page.  You'll notice the page title is "April Fools".  

The logo link which usually goes to index.php was redirected to a fake Cloudflare loading page. Making it appear we were under a DDOS attack.  We were not under any attack. 

We also had a special custom plugin to make it appear you were RepFucked and an angry admin reputation appeared. That is also fake and you are NOT RepFucked. Each member saw their own rep as -10 but everyone else saw your normal reputation.  

Lastly we used April Fools Day to do some maintenance which did require some downtime.  A fake redirect page was added during that time which lead to 0wn3d.txt page by a character named "Mii T. CentOS" which is really just an anagram for Omniscient (yes we're aware it's not 100% correct).  Your data was never in danger or compromised.  

I'm ending the official jokes as of now so I can get some real work done.  I managed to accrue about 400 PMs today which is about 4 times the normal and will take me some time to navigate through them.  On a plus side the maintenance went really well and HF servers were flawlessly updated for performance and security.

Thanks to everyone that participated and enjoy the few pranks we pulled today.

message:
Happy New Year everyone.  I had a great time this week and for New Years I was at a private party even with Katy Perry as the entertainment. It was awesome.  The wife and I had a blast and it was just a magical night full of good food, friends, and the welcoming of a new year.  I hope everyone experienced something similar.

Now for the lowdown.  

First off...member data was in no way compromised.  Not even close. They think they got something they don't really have.  So don't be fooled by screenshots or bullshit.  Your data wasn't taken or accessed in any ways.

So today while having a late breakfast I got some emails about access to accounts and password resets.  These security triggers alerted me pretty quickly that I had a compromise.  A follow up email was sent to me threatening me to ban Orgy or else.  This was about 12:30pm PST give or take 10 mins.  Initially I wasn't sure what was accessed and unfortunately I only had phone access at my location.  But within 30 minutes it was clear I had a breach that needed immediate attention.

I left my breakfast, which looked delicious, and drove home which takes about 30 minutes. Not sure exact time I was home but I'd say maybe 1:30ish.  

I knew the focal point of the breach was my Servage account which hosts Witza.com and as many know I have some emails I use there.  These emails were the key to a few accounts getting compromised.  I'm an avid user of email forwards which actually keeps me more secure and compartmentalizes breaches like these.  I can quickly make adjustments to secure things.

While they had access to Witza.com and the Servage account there is NO USER DATA there and the upgrade and donation pages stem from an unknown host for net.witza.com.  Which was never compromised.   

A defacement page was placed at www.witza.com as well and a tag page which I've kept up:  http://www.witza.com/rofl.php  Congrats to Onionzcrew btw. I'm sure they're super happy they managed to do this.  This really just cost me 2 hours of work and a lost breakfast.  I consider this a very minor breach and I've seen much worse by much better hackers with tons more skillz.  But kudos to them anyways if for nothing more than causing some alarm.

A few members ( Orgy and Diabolic) got rep fucked which can't be undone and some reps were removed from other member accounts too.  

The admincp is htaccess secured and was never accessed.  The staff section requires a password and that also was never access but to be frank with you...the staff section doesn't have anything important in it. It's just staff discussing policies and sometimes a thread to consider new staff.  Very benign stuff.  I don't run a drama queen website.  We don't waste our time trash talking members and stirring up trouble. We're the trouble killers.  

The few accounts compromised from me personally was the PP account which no damage was done and it's fully recovered.  PP was the first phone call I made.

An unused personal Twitter account was stolen and used to update everyone about the compromise.  It's now recovered and all their tweets are deleted except their original tweet. They can keep their shout out trophy.

A digitalocean account was compromised via a PW reset.  I opened a DO account because it was dirt cheap and I wanted to toy around with it.  I have like 10 hosting accounts on various services under aliases and different emails.  There was zilch in the DO account.  Account is also now recovered.

My HF account was compromised with a PW reset as well.  This has the most damaging potential except for the fact our admincp is protected.  And I have lots of safeguards for this contingency anyways.  Very very little damage actually happened.  Of course I was immediately able to fix this and recover the account just fine.

My Coinbase PW was reset but because I have 2FA they couldn't log in.  

My Omniscient Minecraft account was stolen.  They logged into HackerCraft and griefed.  This was probably the only real damage the person did. We have a bit of a problem because it appears the backups stopped working a month ago and I'm not sure what Astonish has done so we can recover. But worse case scenario we just rebuild which was probably going to happen anyways for various reasons.  In a way..they did me a favor.  Silver lining in the clouds and all. Oh and account is recovered too.

During these few hours of the compromise some of my account do have credit cards attached and they might show last 4 digits in the billing page.  This doesn't alarm me.  I won't even bother to change my CC numbers.  I might rotate a few cards, change a few emails, but overall this breach was very minor.  

I know that those who get anything related to me think they've accomplished the climbing of Mt Omni and are heralded for amazing feats of superhuman ability but in this case. It's just not so.  Heck I'm not even embarrassed a slight bit.  Someone managed to get through the security of Servage through social engineering and took the low-hanging fruit.  That stuff is practically a honey trap which gives me lots of alerts of a compromise.  I've lost no accounts. I've not lost 1 cent and other than a couple hours of security work I'm going to go about my day as if this didn't happen. 

Funniest part is they wanted Orgy banned but they rep fucked him and I just reset all his reps.  He has a better rep now than before.  

If anything I'll get extra traffic from the publicity and the drama.  :) 

Any questions?
subject: Happy New Year Breach!

message:
The HF database is NOT dumped or leaked.  

Everyone is aware of the actual HF user table dump that happened a couple years ago. At the time PW were force changed and security measures were put into place.  Everyone was properly notified.

In January the orders database was dumped.  Everyone was informed.  No passwords were part of that dump.

http://pastebin.com/MUNfxRpe

That is NOT HF database accounts.  I suspect it's some site from a member that had their DB dump and you might see one or two familiar usernames. However, I can assure you this is NOT a dump from HF.  

I can tell you this by a number of ways.

1. We require more complex passwords than most of those.
2. Most of the usernames, and I mean most, I couldn't even find on HF.
3. The username "n i g g e r" without spaces is a username we have not allowed on HF since 2010.  

If by chance one or two usernames match an HF user and the password is correct it's because someone is a moron and using the HF password on another site.  You should NEVER EVER EVER UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCE do that.

Make sure on HF you have a UNIQUE password.  

Also note that Pastebin dump is from Nov 3.  I've been told about it multiple times and I'm tired of the rumor being believed.

I've always informed members of any security breach.  And I do investigate even rumors of a breach.  But don't be fooled by those who like to spread lies.

Thank you.
subject: Clarity on Rumor of DB Leak

In an effort to improve searching I've added a nifty SYT button to the forumdisplay page.

You'll see it on the right of the header for each forum marked as SYT next to a Mark button. The Mark button is a simple replacement for the "Mark this forum read" link.  

SYT is Search Your Threads.  Essentially while inside that forum this button will quickly display all your own threads in that particular forum.  This is going to be helpful for those wishing to see new replies to threads they are active in.  No longer do you need the View Your Threads that's on the top to give you results you're not interested in. Just go into a forum (i.e. Lounge) and click it.  You'll get all the threads you have created in the forum.  In the results you can see the arrow next to the thread title for any threads with new replies. The arrow is also a link to the last post you read.

So essentially you should find this as a vast improvement for navigation.

Enjoy.

message:
Because of my new blocks and my new method of getting contacts on blocks I'm getting a lot of feedback from members.  Many want to know why I block countries and ISPs.  They want to know why I throw away traffic and income. 

So today I decided to break the numbers down a bit.

Here is top 10 countries and their upgrade orders these past fews years for upgrades:

US	7449
GB	1583
CA	1087
AU	756
NL	404
SE	347
DK	342
DE	314
FR	246
NO	222


Those are approximate numbers and I won't give the full dates those represent but it's about the last 2-3 years.  Those top 10 countries represent almost exactly 90% of the upgrades.  This means that as long as I don't block those countries we really won't lose too much. Matter of fact if I just whitelisted the top 5 countries we'd likely only lost a few more percent of overall income.    

India you'll notice is not on that list but India represents a healthy amount of overall traffic on the site. 

Here is breakdown of top 10 countries for site traffic which closely resembles the upgrade orders:

1.	 United States	851,107	44.08%	
2.	 United Kingdom	215,178	11.14%
3.	 Canada	130,129	6.74%
4.	 Australia	75,056	3.89%
5.	 India	66,104	3.42%
6.	 Netherlands	61,447	3.18%
7.	 Germany	51,753	2.68%
8.	 Sweden	48,508	2.51%
9.	 France	44,913	2.33%
10.	Denmark	38,590	2.00%

And I highly suspect those making money from the HF Marketplace can likely say this reflects their sales too.  

I do not feel that unblocking countries that we've blocked for years would do anything to change these numbers.  Most got on the block list due to high amounts of fraud orders, scams, ban evaders, and attacks.  All of which we just don't need here.  Also many countries have terrible English skills and we are an English language based site.  Those who can't write in English only lowers the site quality further.

When making decisions on adding or removing countries from the blocklist I do not factor into the equation any personal feelings.  It's not any bias.  It's not because I like or dislike anyone.  It's because I have to weigh the good with the bad and decide if it's worth it. Sometimes it's just not worth allowing a country to remain having access when it's doing nothing but giving me trouble and I spend more time dealing with problems from the region than I am making those who do have access happy.  

And I realize that philosophy can easily mean a few bad apples ruin it for others.  I try to factor that in as well but ultimately there comes a tipping point where 1% of the income or traffic isn't worth the hours upon hours I spend dealing with bullshit.  It's dealing with bullshit which prevents me from getting more features enabled, helping legit members get support, and improving HF overall.  So I must at times make these hard decisions.

Only thing I ask is that members don't take this personal. It's no slight toward any person or group.  

Thank you.

message:
Huge changes to HF serving coming.

Just an update that I'm altering in a significant way how we serve HF.  The changes will increase redundancy, add security, reduce DDOS attack effects, and increase uptime.

We've had some server online for over 2 years and before I had installed some reverse proxy protection the IPs we're known and are still known.  Despite them being known we've had relatively decent uptime as I believe I've made all the proper adjustments to automate attack mitigation.  But despite my best efforts massive attacks as large as 50Gbps disrupt our serving.  I can't have that.

I've already ordered and begun the process of adding a new server that will be a hidden HTTP server.  All the IPs, of which there are many, will always be behind the reverse proxy of Cloudflare or some other DDOS protection service.  SMTP service will be handled completely from a different server/service as well.  

Lastly avatars and signature serving will change. I'm considering using a service like Gravatar for avatars. And of course we already have a significant avatar gallery of our own.  But these will experience changes and don't be surprised if I disable all uploading to the server which also includes attachments.  

These steps are all necessary to increase our security and uptime. Unfortunately attacks persist and because small attacks are ineffective we're experiencing massive attacks that would likely disrupt giant sites like Twitter.  

I will be making these changes this week and I'll update members as things progress and get implemented.

Thank you.
subject: Server Changes For Security

message:
We had an 11 hour downtime due to an attack and the datacenter null routed us incorrectly.  The guy at the datacenter I found out is new and didn't realize the simpler steps he could have taken to deal with the attack and still keep us online.  

The attack was around 30Gpbs so it was substantial size.  I guess he got alarmed and nulled the whole server meanwhile I have so many hidden IPs that we''d have stayed online had he taken different measures.  Instead he removed us completely from the switchport.  

I was offline after about 10pm PDT last night and I guess this happened around 11pm PDT (GMT -8).  I woke up around 7am to a pile of alerts from the monitoring services I have running.  Most of the time these monitoring services API start different security measures automatically to keep us online with just brief interruptions to service.

Of course none of it is effected if we're removed from the swithport.  

So I got up and was like WTF and once I figured out the issue I began working on it right away with the datacenter. It took a lot longer than it should have to get this guy to configure things how I need them but of course eventually he got it right and we're online again.  

Total downtime appears to be about 11 hours. That's 10 1/2 more hours than it should have been.  

The reason this does happen is because we've used this same HTTP server for a few years now.  Early on I did not use Cloudflare server as it was still very new.  Some,but not all, of the server IPs are known and exposed.  I'm well aware of this and normally it doesn't present a huge problem as we have additionally IPs to stay online even if all the known IPs get null routed.  However there is still disruption.

The cure is to get a new server and keep the IPs hidden.  Good news is that I already ordered the server in May and actually just this week began the OS install and service setup.  I still have more fine-tuning like the firewalls, custom kernel, and server hardening to accomplish.  One this new server is in production these types of downtimes will end.  

I'm spreading us out when it comes to serving.  Mail, HTTP, and even image uploading will all get separated to different boxes so that the HTTP server will always stay online.  I'm adding redundancy to every corner of our site.  Even for email I've purchased a package from another company in the event that our smtp server is attacked for an extended period.

The end result is that I expect by Xmas HF will not see any significant downtime from attacks.  

I'm very sorry for todays inconvenience but be aware that I'm working on a solution and these problems will not persist.

Thank you.

HF will always come back online.  Be aware the past 10 days we've been under a very heavy and persistent attack.  Since I've stopped most of the attack with only minor disruptions the attacker(s) has decided to enlarge the scope of the attack.  Today it's effecting us more than I'd like.  I'm okay with downtime but when I'm online and if I can't stop an attack in a reasonable time then I'm alarmed.  

I've spoken a few months ago about changing our setup so we had more uptime.  So even before these attacks I was planning to expand our serving. This past weeks attack just push the time frame to immediate.  I'm ordering new servers today.  I am also investigating multiple ddos prevention solutions.  Hopefully by end of the week we'll be serving from 3 HTTP servers through at least 2 DDOS prevention services.  

Most likely avatar serving will have to be changed and I'll disable avatar uploading as well as attachments. For the 99.9% uptime I expect I think we can all live with those alterations.  

I've not changed HF IPs for years and I'm well aware of the few holes we have in our defenses. Some, but not all, of our IPs are public and well-known.  These do get attacked but filtering normally works to end the attack.  

Apologies to the members for this disruption but I'm working diligently to get it all fixed.  You may see a lot of downtime this next couple days either from attacks or because of serving changes. Please don't be alarmed and be patient.  You can subscribe to our Twitter for the latest updates.

message:
After much debate with staff and reviewing the policy I'm making a statement on the recent questions about site policy for the Gaming tab when it comes to IGM (in game money) for game items.

Much of these issues revolves around Runescape and Minecraft.  These are common games that have IGM. Runescape is even used as a currency outside the game for non-RS items.  Some sellers here on HF take RS points for their sales.

For years now we've had a strict policy that all Marketplace style threads belong within our Marketplace tab.  It was mainly created to avoid the Hacking tab, Computing, and Lounge to be turned into general marketplace areas used more for promotion and sales instead of discussion.

We do allow paid stickies which are often Marketplace style threads but these are often moved back into Marketplace when sticky ends.

When HackerCraft section was added there was allowances and exceptions for trading of IGM for same-game items. I think this was the beginning of some confusion for some members.

The Runescape section is extremely active when it comes to trading of IGM and game items.  But no such official exception was made for that section.  Some weeks ago a thread popped up asking about this.  The result was a subforum was added to RS for Runescape Marketplace which is actually just a redirect to the Virtual Game Item section in the Marketplace tab.

In the RS section itself the rules state:
2. No Marketplace threads. Use the Virtual Items forum.

Some members have received our mandatory 3-day ban (used to be a month btw) for violating this policy then claiming it's not fair or that some other person didn't get banned. 

Action staff decides to take is up to them.  But they work within the guidelines.   You CAN GET BANNED for posting Marketplace threads in the Gaming tab for IGM for game items. I want that to be clear.  

I've asked staff to be lenient when possible but it's the member who takes the chances that gets the risk.  

End result is that there is no actual change in policy and I feel current policies are sufficient to deal with the matter. However staff and I felt some clarification to stop the confusion was in order.

If you want to trade IGM for same game item we still expect the Virtual Game Item forum to be used.  If you want a IRL cash appraisal for a game item it should be in the Marketplace Appraisal section.   

Gaming tab should be about game discussion and shouldn't be turned into a gaming marketplace.

Any questions?

message:
The past week or so HF serving has been poor.  There appears to have been a bug in one of the Apache modules we run. Today I was finally able to track it down and resolve the issue.  

So hopefully those who have experienced problems this past week or two will see those issues fixed.

Basically there was a signal 11 exit for the httpd process.  This meant that a page might not load or a portion wouldn't be fully served. Apache was basically crashing a fork constantly. Often a refresh would fix it but that's not how HF is suppose to be.  

About 2 weeks ago I did some maintenance updating and apparently this bug cropped up.  

In conclusion...we should be all good now. I don't see the error anymore and already I feel the site is serving faster. 

Thank you.

Orders Dump Latest Data (part 3)

This is a continuation thread of "Terrible News".

http://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=3235050  (part 1)
http://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=3235989  (part 2)

I've had a back and forth conversation with the person responsible for the penetration.  While I loathe having to do this I feel it's in the best interest of the community.  I've allowed him to have an open account (still subject to site policies), upgraded him to ub3r, and given him appropriate awards.  In return he's agree to not publically dump the database.  

What that means is most members for now might consider themselves safe.  Currently I'm only aware of a small handful of members who have seen the dump. It's also common knowledge that the group Legion had all their members data released.  So far there appears to be no known public release of the entire DB.  

I'm hoping this move minimizes risk to members.  It may allow them time to change anything they felt could be used against them. Things like email addresses or phone numbers.  Note that I don't recommend you change your phone number unless harassment becomes a problem.  You may consider changing your email on site like PP or your bank if you feel these can be used to steal accounts.  

Members are still at risk of having their data sold or dumped public but I'm hoping the person lives up to the agreement by not releasing the dump public. He has unfortunately stated that he'll likely sell data from the dump one user at a time.  In other words if you have an enemy. They might seek out this person to obtain your oder info.  So please consider how that might effect you.  

In an effort to add more security to this data I'm taking these steps:

1. Random domain at random registrar with random whois.
2. Random host which I currently don't use.
3. Random cloudflare account with random email address.
4. Encrypt the uid table in the database.  

I assume that's enough layers that unless my home computer is compromised (always a possibility) that the data will be near impossible to gather. 

While you would still order at Witza.com the notifications and the database will be somewhere obscure and hidden.  And certain data would be encrypted.  I don't claim this to be a 100% secure method but I honestly can't think of how I would strengthen it beyond these measures.  

Once all this implemented I will announce it along with a coupon for upgrades. I may even step up and release the Pow3r group soon after.  

I seriously thank the many members who have shown support towards HF and me personally.  I was sure we would rebound from this but the great support the community has shown only proves to me that we are a very strong community.

Thanks to everyone.

subject: Terrible News (Continued Part 2)

message:
I have some bad news for the community.  Unfortunately I have no way to make this sound not-so-bad.  It appears that our l33t/ub3r orders database was compromised through an exploit with the host of the database.  It's probably one of the worst things I can tell you has happened. 

The data in our orders database consists of the order first name,last name, address, email, phone, ip, order date, and user id. More or less probably everything needed to DOX thousands of members.  HF accounts themselves are secure.  No passwords are in the DB.

CREDIT CARD DATA was not compromised.  That data is not saved to our orders DB or even viewable by me.  While that's not exactly a silver lining it's at least comforting that you don't have to call your CC company.  Most orders are done through PP anyways.

The data from the theft is very likely going to be used to DOX as I don't see other uses.  We're going to be extra vigilant now in making sure account recovery based on orders also has other verifiable information.  

You might ask how can I let this happen.  I've been pondering an answer to that for hours.  So far I got nothing.  I guess a better question would have been how could I have stopped this from happening.  And to that I still don't know.  Clever hackers have penetrated parts of HF security before.  I'm confident that I took more than reasonable steps to secure the data.  Giant companies like Sony experience deep penetrations.  We all are vulnerable to a degree and HF is no exception.  

If you wonder why we have this data it's to ensure that upgrades are legitimate, not fraudulent, and that members are not ban evading.  There is no other option at this time but to save this data.  I am however reviewing options available to obsfucate or encrypt the data.

I found out about this on Jan 26, 2013.  I immediately investigated to confirm the validity.  I spent hours making adjustments to secure the data.  

I expect uproar over this.  I'm not looking forward to the backlash at all.  However I feel it's my responsibility to alert the community about this breach.  If you're wondering what steps you should now take.  The answer is, I don't know.  There is likely nothing you can do about this.  We are at the mercy of person(s) that took the data.  This person is a known blackhat who's been repeatedly banned from this community.  The people who have access are not do-gooders. They will likely use this data to threaten and harass members.  

I know many of you are probably feeling deep disappointment.  To you I say, I'm sorry and I deeply regret that this has happened.  I have no way to fix this. I have no way to undo it.  

HF has recovered from some fairly damaging penetrations before including a full user table dump in Feb 2011.  We will recover from this too.  

I will do my best to answer questions now. I know there will be those of you upset over this. I just ask that you be respectful in tone.  I take this incident extremely seriously and no one is more upset by this than I am.

message:
Apparently about 90 7:25am PST the HF MySQL server crashed.  It's unknown to me at this time why that occurred but my guess is that it's time to add more resources to MySQL such as RAM.  We currently run 24GB on the server and the database is using 22GB now.  Since we run InnoDB tables it's very memory intense.  I can easily upgrade us to 48GB and give MySQL all the memory it wants.

The server hasn't crashed in a very long time.  Maybe this is just an anomaly but I'll keep a close watch.  

Good news is that I was up at 8:30am and caught this quick.  Oh joy.

Thanks for reading.
subject: MySQL Crashed and Downtime

message:
I think it's time I expand HF serving once again. Even though we're under DDOS protection, filters, and firewalls some of our old IPs (not all) are public.  They cause disruption to our serving with massive attacks (3gb+) and while I can adjust and mitigate these they still manage to cause slight downtime and slow serving down.

I'm probably going to take some final steps to end this type of attack by ordering 3 new servers.  One for mail and two more for apache/nginx.  We'd have somewhere around 24 IPs to serve HF from. Of course this will increase our serving costs but these things are necessary.

Cloudflare does an amazing job of hiding our IPs as well as deflecting DDOS attacks. But a select few of our IPs are public and they are used to attack.  With a new set of servers and IPs these attacks will be mitigated.

Currently HF has 2 servers and a CDN.  After expansion we'd have 4 servers and the CDN.  

btw here is last 30 days bandwidth to give you some idea of what I'm talking about. 

[img]http://i.minus.com/i5VsgNdKDOfaU.PNG[/img]

message:
http://hackforums.net/gauth.php

This is something I started working on before I broke my hand and I wanted done for the summer. But I'm happy to say today I devoted the necessary time to code out a nice beta test.

It's rough but the idea is to test the functionality of adding Google Authenticator to the site.  

In case you do not know what Google Authenticator is. It's an App by Google for 2FA (two-factor authentication).  It can greatly help to protect accounts.

For many with Google accounts you may already be familiar with the application.
You can read a bit about it here:  http://support.google.com/a/bin/answer.py?hl=en&answer=1037451

If this beta is a success I'll expand the usage so that P0W3R users (yes that's coming soon) will be able to have a higher form of account security. And this is not likely going to be the only option.

With the 2FA Gauth I'll be able to require it for say...login, username change, email change, or password change. Settings will depend on a number of factors.  

Again this is VERY basic but should function without any problems.  It currently does not protect any accounts.

Also note. This does not require you to provide us your phone number or any type of access which might compromise your security or private information.  It's basically an encryption app with a constantly changing code.

The Google Authenticator app is available on various platforms:
http://support.google.com/accounts/bin/answer.py?hl=en&answer=1066447

You are required to have a camera/barcode scanner at this time but I might adjust it so that you can also manually enter a code.

We'd be the first MyBB site to offer such a feature and I'm not releasing this public.  HF will start being unique again and all the wannabe's can kiss my ass.

So anyways...ub3rs feel free to beta test this and ask any questions.

message:
https://www.cloudflare.com/business

So should HF pay $200 per month for the CF business pro?  

I feel it would stop all DDOS attacks when enabled as they have a 100% guaranteed uptime.

They offer layer 7 protection as well as layers 3 and 4.  We already mitigate level 3 and 4 locally pretty well.  Layer 7 attacks are sometimes but not always stopped at the network level.

But having CF as a double layered protection imho would go a long way to keeping us online 99-100% vs the 98% uptime we currently have.

I would not keep it enabled all the time. Currently I only use CF service under certain attacks as just part of my mitigation scheme. If we go business plan then I'd opt to use it more often.  

Also Railgun is kind of hot.
https://www.cloudflare.com/railgun

The biggest issue I have with CF is that I can't block the massive amounts of proxy/VPNs that I do now.  Unsure if their business plan will allow me to install my 8000 line list of cidr blocks.

We settled on a compromise that I would promote his new site in exchange for advertising money which was already a deposit made to buy HF.  We had met here in Vegas and he stated he was from Ukraine...had the accent too.  I never got the impression he was anyone but who he said he was.  I assisted with the setup of CPF by installing some plugins and building their theme. After a few months I told the owner I didn't want to be involved anymore and that I filled my obligation.  

So HF was never sold and I'm still the owner to this day. I really honestly can't say if he was FBI himself, turned at some point, or maybe the site was seized.  I just don't know beyond what I read in the FBI report today.

My gut aches at this news.  It's very unfortunate that I somehow got involved. That being said HF is not a BH site and I don't pity people who take chances the way those who were arrested have.   I've never wanted that type of activity here and now you know why. It's very dangerous. HF is an open forum where posts are not hidden and anyone can join. You're a real dumb ass to admit to anything here.

I've closed the account of the owner of the UC FBI site.  All his IP connections seem to be socks. He was never a very active member here but did ask me MyBB questions every now and then. He was an ub3r as a courtesy. I did meet the guy and he did pay me good money in cash.  One thing makes sense to me now though.  When he was going to buy HF he said he was going to delete the site and start over with a BH Carding site.  I told him that was a terrible idea but he gave the excuse he wanted a more exclusive site. Eventually his idea to start a new site with my help was formed.  Makes me wonder if there wasn't some legal reason like entrapment to delete the existing site.

I'm a bit overwhelmed by this.  I'm not sure what to believe. It's been over 18 months since I last even had a PM with the guy. The person I met didn't feel suspicious to me.  I feel like I'm in some story or movie right now.  All so odd. I can only imagine how crazy things would be if I really did sell HF back then to this guy.  

You can btw read the original thread about the sale and promotion of his site here:
http://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=474743

Some are questioning if they should remain members of HF.  And I think if you're doing something here that you're concerned about then maybe you should leave. Because as always I'm not here to protect you.  I don't encourage using computers for illegal activity and if that's what you're doing then that's your problem. My legal disclaimer is simple. I will not share your private member data without a valid US Court subpoena. 

http://hackforums.net/misc.php?action=help&hid=12
"We do not share this information with outside parties except to the extent necessary when the law requires us to comply."

I take sharing of private member data very very seriously. Anyone in staff can confirm this and anyone who's ever tried to get me to give up an IP or email knows that too.  

I will not host HF offshore either. It wouldn't make any difference anyways because I'm a U.S. citizen subject to US laws.  You joined a U.S. hosted site. 
 
Please note that it doesn't seem like any HF members who were not members of CPF were arrested.  It does seem specific that members of that site are the ones at risk.  If HF was an FBI operation or under investigation I think we'd be closed down today.  HF is not imho at risk of being shut down. I take great pains to make sure we operate within legal limits.  I personally do not participate in any computer crime whatsoever.  I'm the admin here and give customer support for upgrades and stickies.  

Another thing...I haven't mentioned or advertised CPF for years now.    Over the years people have been arrested that are indeed members of HF.  I don't find that shocking considering that the arrest rate is about 5% of americans are arrested at some point.  We've seen members post about DUI, robberies, and of course cyber crime charges. Seems only about 2-3 actual HF members are involved in this report. Out of 300k members and after 5+ years only a few arrested and those were actually from ANOTHER forum does not add up to me being directly involved.  It just doesn't.  Believe what you want but I had zero knowledge about these arrests.

I've stated numerous times that I was sure and still sure that we have law enforcement as members here.  I wouldn't doubt they have accounts on just about every hacking, cracking, warez, or carding forum that exists.  

I've deactivated the Blackshades private forum for now. Unsure what I'll do about the group.  It's likely the owner of the group won't be around for a while...if ever. Considering the report I just read about the owners arrest I think it's best to remove the forum section.

Ugh...what a mess this is. I completely understand member concerns though.  Unsure if my statement has helped any but it's everything I know at this time. Fuck this sucks.  But I think just like the gazillion other dramas of HF this will pass in a week and we'll all be doing what we normally do.  Other than the drama this has created 0 change in my day.

Well on the bright side those who DDOS HF might think twice now. 

I'll leave this thread open and try to answer questions but I won't tolerate being disrespected. You're warned.

message:
For the past month or two we've had a lot of bots hitting the profiles page.  Fake accounts were made and then the profile pages botted.  I think to obtain all the username or whatever other profile info was there.  

People are clever and think of some interesting techniques to mess with the site and members.

So today I saw some unusual DB activity and lo and behold it's member login attempts.  I think someone has matched the year old DB dump with some good-ole brute force and working through a rainbow dictionary grabbing whatever accounts they can.  

Fortunately just days after learning our user table was dumped I took quick action. All the regular accounts without activity were closed.  All ub3r/l33t accounts had a forced password change.  That was a very time consuming month of recovering accounts.

It does seem though that these new login attempts are related but something different too.  Tracing the logins almost all the accounts are already closed.  Some are not but I've closed them manually as I find them being logged into.

But that's not enough.  So I also created a nice plugin that will log login attempts.  With that info I compare how many accounts an ip is attempting to login to.  If an IP is trying to login to multiple accounts I will know and the plugin will block the login.  

I wanted to inform members because some accounts might get stolen.  Very few but still some. Also as a precaution accounts we see logged into from these bots will be either closed or banned to protect the account and the community. Use contact form for Stolen/Lost Account to recover.

Also for those using proxies or VPNs to login.  If you have a shared IP then you may not be able to login as the plugin is going to flag you and deny the login. You also might trigger a ban. Be careful.

I thank everyone for their patience as a few errors occurred while implementing the plugin.

message:
I've decided to test Cloudflare services.  The reason behind such action is an attempt to thwart some of the larger DDOS attacks we've been experiencing.  I've known about and have been using Cloudflare for months at site like SF, Witza, and Central. It's been effective but at times buggy.  However I feel the potential benefits outweigh the problems.  

I contacted Cloudflare support over a week ago requesting information about handling HF and our 40 million monthly page views site. They assured me their service can handle it.  Last night we experienced large attacks again and I felt I had nothing to lose by trying Cloudflare.  

I'm aware of the pitfalls that using CF will bring.  I've already begun to make firewall adjustments and changes to HF files in order to lessen these effects.  

But the benefits of using CF are huge.  They act as a reverse proxy and a WAF.  They have geo tools for blocking countries built in.  And they offering caching of content.  

One of the negatives of course is less control. If they go down we go down.  And there is that annoying captcha they throw up every now and again.  But we go down sometimes regardless.

DNS changes were made in order to use Cloudflare service. For some that can't connect it's because of that reason.  So if you can view www but not hacforums.net that's DNS problems and will eventually resolve itself.

At this time I've lowered some of the CF security settings until we can flush out some issues. Their Challenge Passage TTL I have set to 1 day. I'd disable it but they don't have that option. I did customize the page but that might not take hold for hours.

In short we're aware of some Cloudflare problems today.  We can only wait it out and see if it improves.  Cloudflare Pro is only costing me $5 a month since I already have 2 other sites as Pro.  So cost wise it's a no-brainer. Some of the other reliable reverse proxy DDOS protections I have seen start at $300 and go to $5000 a month.  A cost I've not yet decided we need just because we go down a few hours every now and then.  But I will continue to make adjustments to keep us online.

So please just be patient.  You don't need to make a new thread evertime CF pop you an error.  I will be closely monitoring activity and how CF handles our site.

message:
1. Lulz Sec did not compromise our DB.  They only put it in their torrent which made it very popular as a download.

2. DB was compromised via a shell on Feb 19, 2011.  I know who did it and I know how they did it. The exploit is fixed.  The people who actually did shell us have never claimed responsibility in public and I don't name names.

3. Recent downtime from DDOS attacks are from a few parties but overall the downtimes were in part because of network problems related to changes in our setup. Not to say we can't be taken down but not all downtimes are because of significant attacks.

4. The question some ask is why didn't I do a full password reset when I found out the DB was leaked.  It's a good question.  At the time I felt MOST accounts were secured and I wanted to figure out some good methods to deal with a situation like this.  I'm extremely busy all the time.  I knew the best solution was a full scale password reset like we have now.  So in the end it didn't matter if I reset all PW's then or now. Eventually it had to be done.  Do I wish I did it before?  Not really. I personally don't think it matters too much. In the end I had to do this anyways and accounts are not lost.

5. People are asking if their info is secured.  The short answer is no.  The DB contained your  registration IP, last active IP (from feb 19), email, usernotes, and password hash. If any of that data being exposed represents a security risk to you then take appropriate measures.

6. Recent accounts signed up after Feb 19 are secure. They are not compromised. I believe it's around uid 687,123 (confirmed). So if you have a uid after that you're fine.

7. This is not the end or downfall of HF.  It's a disruption.  That's it. All upgraded accounts are secured and currently being recovered.  Many inactive accounts have been placed into DEAD group.  Many other passwords even on regular accounts were force changed.  We get attacks, downtimes, and even get hacked every now and again.  It happens.  We're a huge target.  My promise to you is that HF will always come back online. Activity on the site today is just as good as it was a week ago. This is the only post I'm going to make about this. I will not allow groups hoping to make a name for themselves use attacks against me or our community as a way to gain fame.  

Today a group defaced and deleted a handful of site in my network.  It was a very simple compromise as I don't spend all day long securing those sites.  I know exactly how they entered.  It will get fixed and no data was lost.

Taking down my network sites is like beating up my 12 year old and claiming that I'm weak.  It goes to show a juvenile attitude and my guess is that those in the group responsible are children themselves.  No adult with any maturity would act in such a manner.  

Staff is instructed to junk all posts related to this incident. It's not even directly related to HF. This is more of a personal attack against me.  Nothing new really. Instead they target me in a clear attempt to gain notoriety.  I'm personally not impressed.

message:
There is a shroud of secrecy that is my Ub3r requirements.  

I'm going to openly state that I'm not publishing my ub3r requirements for a very good reason.  I think it's a measure of a member that instead they produce what they feel is their best foot forward.  Whether it's a simple "requesting ub3r" or some long drawn out PM about their qualifications.  For some being accepted into the ub3r group is important. It might be a personal goal, it could be for freebies, maybe they just want rep power, or they're involved in Marketplace and feel ub3r will help them.

I don't fault anyone for wanting to be in the ub3r group.  Is it the most elite group? No. It's not.  But there are benefits. Obvious benefits are just extra forum abilities. Lots of members want to tear others down for no good reason.  Some are even passionate about knocking down the ub3r group.  It's just silly to say ub3r means nothing.  It obviously does mean SOMETHING and probably something different to everyone.  

I have a philosophy and a mentality about what I expect for people to be in the ub3r group.  It's not about ass kissing. It's not about being a donator.  There is one main question I ask.  [b]Is this member likely to do harm to HF?[/b]  I figure that out by reviewing some things.  And to be honest if I can't answer the question with a no then they are denied.  So if you get denied. It's because I think at some level you're potentially harmful to the community or I'm simply unsure of your intent.

If I was to ever publish some list of requirements then those wishing to do harm would simply game the system. If I said you have to have 100 positive reps, 250 posts, and be a member for 3 months then that's what every scammer would do.  Instead you gotta pass my very unique smell test. 

Not to say my method is 100% effective and that those in ub3r group are trustworthy but up till they are accepted I don't feel they are bad for the community.  Most bad activity begins once they are in the group.  And even in some cases I've booted people.  Certainly a lot of ub3r get temp banned. I think most quickly learn being in ub3r is not protection from staff or a license to break policies.  

So anyways I was inspired to make this post. I hope it helps some of you understand some things.

message:
There has always been times when a member decides to go out in a blaze of glory.  I use this term to describe it when a member creates a thread going all out on the site, staff, policy or even me.  They rant about how the sites run poorly. How new members are low quality.  How some new policy is complete shit.  Or maybe that scammers run HF and all I care about is money.  

These members are trolls.  They are making their last posts knowing they will get banned.  These are often long-term or even well-reputed members.  For many reasons they've decided that it's time they leave HF and instead of simply logging out and moving on they decide to get one last rant about everything they don't like about HF.  

These events are often triggered by a rep fuck, ban, new policy, or a recent scam.  They feel disgruntled and want to be heard.  They want to express their anger.  It's understandable but let's be honest. It's not productive.  It's actually counter-productive as few of these threads produce anything of value.  The same complaints are made and even if they are valid complaints there are rarely anything constructive about how to cope and correct these problems.  

I hold no ill-will toward members that want to leave or have a grievance. But you contact me personally if you want to take stab at me.  Creating a public thread in an attempt to gain member support is cowardly.  I won't stand for a mob mentality rising up against my policies or how this site is run.  HF is not a dictatorship. HF is not a democracy. HF is not a government. It's a website I personally own that is a large and active community.  I've never advertised it as anything else.  With 200,000 members this place cannot be run by members.  One person must make decisions. 

Ultimately I'm the only guy that faces consequences based on the sites failure or success in policies. If I make members happy I make more money. If I piss off the community I make less money.  So my intention is never to make less money.  It's to grow this community as best I can.  This goal doesn't always make all members happy. It's inevitable that a certain group is going to get ticked off at my actions.  However I'm not going to pander to a select few members. I'm going to focus on the overall community. Even if these few are vocal and don't recognize why certain policies are vital to the sites longevity.

I'm aware of problems here.  I know full well our weak points.  I've read every complaining rant.  I'm not so arrogant to think HF is perfect.  Matter of fact all the problems we have plague me daily but solutions aren't nearly as easy as stating the problems we have. Solutions for members mean less problems for me.  So finding solutions is ultimately very important to me personally.

With all that said. I think it's time to officially ban these "Blaze of Glory" threads.  I'm tired of attention seeking disgruntled members deciding they're going to attack this community, me, and staff.  End result is always the same. Their account banned.  So I'm officially banning these threads and the only course of action will be the perma banning of the account and the junking of the thread.  They only create drama and serve no positive purpose here.  

I'm sure some will express how this isn't fair or that I'm trying to stop complaints.  That's not it.  There are ways to express a problem and offer suggestions to improve HF.  I even opened the suggestions area a few weeks ago.  So that argument is null.  I'm not trying to control speech either. I'm just tired of the drama stirred up by disgruntled members on their way out.  

If you feel yourself coming to the edge. Here is a solution.  Log out. Come back if you want at later time or don't.  But when you go out in a Blaze of Glory you can kiss your account good bye.

Thank you.

message:
What a day this is turning out to be.  

Since rumors are likely to spread and I think this info will be public soon anyways I'm going to announce it to everyone.

Back in February 2011 we were shelled.  Yes that's right.  We were shelled.  We are not impenetrable and have no golden lock on our server/website. 

I became aware of the shells weeks ago while reviewing server files.  It was a very alarming moment of course.  Site was shut down for "maintenance" and I started reviewing logs and other forensics were done.  Ultimately I found out who uploaded the shells but their English was terrible and they didn't really provide me much info.  

I believe the shells were updated from a MyBB exploit just before it was patched.
http://blog.mybb.com/2011/02/22/mybb-1-6-2-and-1-4-15-security-update/

All evidence points to a XSS vulnerability in modcp that is now patched. 

I had previously no evidence that the shells were used maliciously or that data was stolen.  The penetrators are still members here and I hold no ill will against them. They had the shells up for weeks without any real damage to the site.  

However the real question remained.  Did they grab the database?  I wasn't sure. They weren't saying.  It did not seem appropriate to alarm the member base without knowing more information.  We have too many members to just change all passwords. Also all passwords in the DB are encrypted and salted. Which means any passwords harder than "password" or "pass123" won't be easy to crack.  Given that we force complex passwords anyone having the DB shouldn't be easily able to grab accounts.  

But there are other concerns.  Like grabbing members emails and IPs.  I do take member privacy and security seriously.  Today is the first time I've had any evidence our data was compromised.  So now you're being informed.  

Today a member is boasting about having access to the DB.  So someone or some group may be releasing it public.  After reviewing data given I've been convinced it's valid and it's from the time period I know we were shelled.  

If you'd like to change your password or email now is the time to do it.  While I'm firmly convinced accounts are safe that doesn't mean you're not exposed somewhere else.

I'm really not looking forward to posting this but I believe it's the right thing to do.  Let's see how it goes.

message:
OMG. You have got to be kidding me.

Most everyone read this thread:
http://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=1112217

We had a bad weekend with our DB server.  That thread explains how our DB tables became corrupt and I had to revert to backup. In the thread I eventually explain how I'm getting a new SSD drive, backup NAS, and more ram for the server.  

The NAS backup was installed Monday afternoon and I quickly threw a Monday 4am backup onto it.  Worked great.  

The SSD and ram were going to be added at 10pm PST. It was all scheduled and I was really happy about the new upgrades.  

10pm came and the work began. I say we were down 30 minutes before server came back online.  My next job was to mount new SSD drive then move the DB datadir to the new drive for the boost in performance.  

That's where it began to go wrong.  When I attempted a dump I had 2 tables go bad on me.  One was a mod log table.  The other was the posts table (uh oh).  The mod logs I just truncated. I didn't need them anways.  The rest of the tables backed up just fine.  So I began to try and figure out how to fix my posts table.  

Two hours later and not a hint of success I was forced to make the same decision I made yesterday.  To revert to the Monday 4am backup.  I was even scared it would not work.  However I think the NAS saved us.  The revert went fine and we're back online.  

Fact is I think the drive we have is having hardware failure.  I'm sure it's exacerbated by our extremely active website. But I was having I/O errors on just moving the raw mybb_posts.ibd file.  It was a 5.3GB file but the mybb_moderator table was tiny.

How I'm going to deal with this is unknown. I'm hoping our new clean drive and NAS will keep us from losing data.  But I'm not sure. If more problems continue I'll have to ask datacenter to replace this drive and rebuild this server. That's a potential nightmare for me. I just don't have the time to do that.  

My next step is to create a strong backup scenario where the NAS is used twice daily.  

I know all this sucks. We lose a day of posts then the next day we lose another 16 hours of posts.  I'm rather pissed about it but I'm actually very tired at the moment and need some sleep.  

I wish this had gone differently but it is what it is.  I feel that if I didn't get that extra drive and NAS today we might have had a much bigger problem on our hands.  Yes we lost some data. But some data is better than a lot of data.  

So let's get past this and move on. I'm too tired to hold a grudge against the server.

EDIT: Made a video.
[yt]http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P-BduK2t-wE[/yt]
subject: Part 2 Of The DBZ Saga

I've renamed our Scam Reports forums to be Deal Disputes. I feel it's a more accurate representation of the section.  The word "scam" or "scammer" doesn't always apply to a deal gone bad.  When two parties make an agreement and if one is not satisfied there is this automatic mentality that a person was scammed.  A real scam requires intent.  What that means is that before the deal is even made one party in the deal had already decided he was going to break the agreement. By either not paying, paying with fraudulent funds, disputing payment, or not providing the product or service.  However deals can go wrong for a lot more reasons. Buyers can be morons,  PP payments can be placed on hold, instructions and ebooks can be bad quality.  

So the end result of my diatribe is that I felt it was time to rename Scam Reports to something more well-rounded.

Thank you.

message:
Ode to MySQL

Oh MySQL you database server
I stare at your process
I am your only observer
I spend my days reading your logs
Because I know you're a resource hog
You hold my data to keep it light
Then you crash and burn
Each and every night
You are my friend and my enemy
I need you and hate you
At times I don't understand you
But in the end you're what I need
Hopefully some day I will succeed


So today as many know MySQL crapped out.  This was no attack. It was a basic oversight on my part in my mysql setup. I had not set an expire time for the bin logs. A 200GB HD drive partition maxed out last night around 3am.  So once the drive was full mysql couldn't finish any queries and so locked up displaying the max connections error.  I'm very glad that I understand all this crap because it didn't take me long to fix it.  We're back up and running just fine now and this problem will not occur again.

Sorry and thanks,
Omni

P.S. Hope you like my prose.
subject: Ode to MySQL

It appears that we've hit another growth spurt during December.  I'm not sure if it's because our new DB server allowed for more reliable page views or if the xmas break gave us a boost. Probably a little of both.  

Our oldest server in the set of 3 I have is our webserver. It runs our firewall, mail, and http needs.  Mail and firewall are a fairly small footprint but obviously http (Apache) is the main load.

I sit and watch the servers from SSH every day.  I thought we had maybe up till 6 months before we would need a new webserver.  I toying with many ideas such as running a reverse proxy or maybe Nginx.  Today we've hit a record for most users online; ignore the current record stat.  It's pushed up the time table for a new webserver.  

Whenever we hit a new record it's inevitable that a month or two later to be the norm.  We are seriously headed to be a top 1000 website on the internet.  I'm not sure how that's possible but every passing month that appears to be more likely.  I'm stoked and I'm scared shitless at the same time. 

Statistically we've grown with traffic by 30% since September 2010.  You're probably noticing lag today and even bad page loads.  This is where we're headed. Lots of downtime if I don't start planning this now. Kind of a shocker to me really that so quickly we need a new webserver but the needs of this site have always surprised me.  We grow really fast. 

Please don't take this post as a call for fundraising either.  Our current donation and member upgrade level are sufficient to pay for a new server.  So please don't think I'm begging for quick donations.  I'm not.  This is more about informing members about what's going on and what I'm doing to fix it.

message:
We are now on our new DB server.  After waking up to see how laggy HF was I restarted mysql.  Apparently we reached our ceiling on this server as the DB was unable to handle the load of the DB size (nearly 5.5GB) and the traffic.  Weekends around here are very busy.  I tried for nearly 2 hours to get us online but table locks on the posts table were too much.  After much frustration I knew the time had come.  

I had already begun working on the new server by setting up FreeBSD and getting some of my custom tools installed.  I would estimate I was 40% done. I was hoping to be about 80% and then actually close HF and do the move.  Today I was not given that option.  I turned HF off and asked members to visit SupportForums.net while I worked.  I worked fast and I worked hard and after about 5 hours of downtime we are now back online running from the new server.  

Currently our DB is one a single server again. I am hoping to run the configuration in a master/slave mode but I actually may just turn off old server and get another server instead.  I have a lot of research ahead of me concerning this.  The new server has 18gb ram and old server was only 8gb.  New server is a dual quad-core (8 cores) while old server was single quad-core (4 cores).  So even though we are once again on a single server, this single server is more than twice the power.  The additional ram is very important to DB usage as we have 3GB in Innodb tables.  It's very likely I will be converting our mybb_posts table from MYISAM to InnoDB in the near future. I would do it today but I feel we've had enough downtime for one afternoon.

I'd like to thank every single member that helped with contributions toward the new DB server. In particular I'd like to thank [url=http://hackforums.net/member.php?action=profile&uid=80618]Nokia2mon[/url]. He's donated a significant amount of money for HF servers and has now bought over 100 members upgrades to l33t/ub3r.  He runs contests so please don't PM beg him. Find his threads for his contest if he's running any.

Of course I'll be watching very carefully the new DB server but I think we're good.  We won't know for a week or so how well this new server does but initially I'm very happy with results.

So what's next for HF?  I'll do a simple breakdown of things that I need to do.

1. Upgrade us to MyBB 1.6x.
2. Review new HF and MyBB features for implementation
3. Setup a new HTTP server (nginx possibly) as our current one is also buckling from the load


On a related note: I've deleted all Junk posts (not ub3r junks) since we needed to save room from 500,000 posts.  I realize that it's an immense amount of posts.  There are forums out there that would have died to have this many posts and we just deleted them and it barely made a dent in our overall totals.  But of course this requires me to do a post recount.  So if you see your post count dramatically lower. That's why. The new count is accurate. Your old count was not. There are some MyBB anomolies that cause inconsistencies. But I can't regularly do a post count as it takes about an hour to do it. It's cumbersome.

Thanks everyone.

message:
Considering the 3 threads so far about unbanned members I guess I'll have to address the issue.  

Every so often I have an amnesty where we clear out the ban list.  This is I believe is the 4th amnesty since HF started.  

The reasons behind the amnesty are a few.  

1. Some members deserve a second chance. I'd like to think of myself as forgiving.
2. Some members might have been wrongly banned (it happens).
3. Many banned accounts are members who will just never return anyways.
4. The overhead for the banned members.  It's in the datacache table and we had about 1700 members in the list. That's a lot of data in cache constantly being grabbed. We now have 500 members and saves space and should help slightly with load times.
5. I don't like having a 5000 banned member list.  That's where it would be if I didn't do this.

Now with all those reasons I think you see why it was done.  The negatives are that some unbanned might cause some problems. The amnesty doesn't stop us from banning them again. 

As a precaution I personally went through the list and anyone banned for scamming was either perma banned, given negative reputation, or rep fucked.  This should help ensure scammers are either known or not welcomed back. This took me hours and you can see on the bans list (ub3r can) that 500 people are still banned most with the label of scammer.  

Guys like bracco just got butthurt, spammed, and were banned.  Technically not a reason he isn't eligible for amnesty.  If he or anyone unbanned wants to act the fool they'll be banned again.  Not an issue at all.

On another note I'd like to ask anyone with multiple accounts to PM me profiles links.  I'm going to try to merge accounts for banned members.  If you're not an unbanned member but have multiple accounts this is your chance to get that fixed by PM'ing me the accounts.  There will be no penalty at this time but this offer is only good for one week. After that if staff sees you have multiple accounts you'll probably be banned.  Be aware I need proof that it's your account. Proof would be order IDs or matching IPs.  I won't merge unless I can actually verify that it's your account.

Thank you.
